Arne Jacobsen: the Series 7 and Ant chairs by Fritz Hansen, also still in production
Børge Mogensen: solid oak and leather chairs and sofas, many made by Fredericia
Niels O. Møller: dining chairs by J.L. Møllers, often sold in sets
Kai Kristiansen and Arne Vodder: teak and rosewood sideboards and cabinets
Grete Jalk and Illum Wikkelsø: lounge chairs and sofas

sections.heading: Marks, labels and construction
paragraphs: Look for a maker's stamp or brand burnt into the wood, a metal tag, or a paper label under seats and inside drawers and doors. Many Danish pieces carry a round Danish Furniture Makers Control label, which confirms Danish production but not a specific designer. Ask for photos of all of these.

Construction tells you a lot too. Better Danish pieces use dovetailed drawers, solid wood edges on veneer, and neatly finished backs and insides. A sideboard with a hardboard back nailed on and plastic drawer runners is unlikely to be a high end Danish piece, whatever the description says.

sections.heading: Teak, oak and rosewood
paragraphs: Teak is the most common wood and the easiest to look after: clean it, then apply teak oil sparingly. Oak pieces, especially from Mogensen and Wegner, are often solid and very durable.

Rosewood (palissander) pieces are more valuable and need care. Brazilian rosewood is a protected species under international trade rules, and selling or exporting furniture made from it can require documentation. If you plan to resell abroad, ask what paperwork the seller has, and if none, price that risk in.

sections.heading: Condition checks
paragraphs: Veneer damage is the main problem: lifted edges, water stains, sun bleaching and deep scratches. Small issues can be fixed by a restorer, but a stripped and heavily varnished top loses much of the look. Chairs should have firm joints with no wobble; reglueing a Danish dining chair properly costs money.
Check paper cord seats on Wegner and Møller chairs. Replacing a worn cord seat by a specialist is common and affordable compared with the chair, but it adds to your total.

sections.heading: Finding good pieces
paragraphs: Search with designer and model names, and also with plain descriptions: teak dressoir schuifdeuren, palissander kast, eetkamerstoelen teak. Older sellers often do not know the maker, and their prices reflect that. On vindje.com you can ask for something like a teak sideboard around 180 cm long with sliding doors and a maker's label, and the search reads the descriptions for you.
Be realistic about bargains. Dealers watch Marktplaats closely, and a labelled Wegner chair at a low price rarely stays listed for long. Message quickly and be ready to pick up.

price_guide.item: Teak sideboard, Danish style, unknown maker
Set of 4 Niels O. Møller dining chairs

faq.q: How can I tell if furniture is genuinely Danish?
faq.a: Look for a maker's stamp, a metal tag or a Danish Furniture Makers Control label, and check construction quality. Without marks, Deens design in a listing only describes a style.

faq.q: Is vintage teak furniture still a good buy?
faq.a: Good teak pieces are durable and easy to maintain, and unbranded ones are often reasonably priced. Labelled designer pieces have risen in price and are bought quickly.

faq.q: How do I care for a teak sideboard?
faq.a: Dust it, clean it with a mildly damp cloth, and apply a thin coat of teak oil once or twice a year. Keep it away from radiators and direct sun.

faq.q: Can I sell rosewood furniture abroad?
faq.a: Furniture made from Brazilian rosewood can need paperwork for trade or export. Check the current rules before buying a rosewood piece to resell outside the Netherlands.

example_wish: Danish teak sideboard about 180 cm long with sliding doors, maker's label visible, veneer in good condition, under 800 euro, anywhere in the Netherlands

title: How to spot replica designer furniture in a listing
meta_title: How to spot replica designer furniture in a listing
description: Learn to spot replica designer furniture on Marktplaats from the listing alone: price, wording, photos, labels and seller patterns, before you travel.
intro: You can spot most replica designer furniture without leaving home. Price, a few telling words, the kind of photos and the seller's other listings give it away. The ones that get through are fakes with copied labels, and for those you need receipts and close-up photos.

sections.heading: Start with the price
paragraphs: Designer originals keep a large share of their value second hand. A design that costs EUR 900 new and sells used for EUR 80 is almost always a copy. Look up the current new price from the official maker, then expect a used original in decent condition at roughly 40-70 percent of that.
A low price is not always a scam. Inheritances and house clearances produce genuine bargains. But if the price is low and the photos also look off, the price is telling you something.

sections.heading: Words that give it away
paragraphs: Read the title and description slowly. Sellers who know they have a copy often say so in softer words.
bullets: stijl, style, look, a la, geinspireerd door, in de geest van
replica, reproductie, kopie, design klassieker without a maker
Only the designer's name, never the maker (for example Eames but no Vitra)
Nieuw in doos, multiple colours available, or meerdere op voorraad
No dimensions, no age, no story of where it was bought

sections.heading: What the photos tell you
paragraphs: Stock photos copied from a webshop are a warning sign. Ask for photos taken in the seller's home, including the underside and any labels. Compare proportions with photos on the official maker's site: copies often get leg thickness, seat height or the angle of the backrest slightly wrong.

Look at the materials. Classic giveaways are glossy plastic where the original is matt, painted metal where the original is chromed or polished, leather that looks flat and uniform, and visible welds or screws where the original has clean joints. Colours that the maker never offered are another clue.

sections.heading: Labels, receipts and serial numbers
paragraphs: Most current makers mark their products: Vitra, Knoll, Fritz Hansen, Cassina, Carl Hansen and others use stamps, embossing, labels or certificates. Ask which one applies to the item and request a clear photo.

Better copies sometimes carry fake labels, so treat a label as one piece of evidence. An original invoice from a known dealer, a certificate with a serial number, or wear that matches the stated age all add up. A seller with a genuine piece will usually be happy to show proof.

sections.heading: Check the seller's profile
paragraphs: Click through to the seller's other listings. A private person selling one chair because they are moving looks different from an account with ten identical Barcelona chairs in different colours. The second is a shop, usually selling new replicas, even if it is listed as private.

Also check how long the account has been active and whether the location matches the pickup address. If you are filtering a lot of listings, vindje.com can be told to skip anything described as style, replica or inspired by, which cuts the noise before you start checking details.

sections.heading: Most copied designs to be careful with
paragraphs: Some designs are copied far more than others. With these, assume a copy until shown otherwise: Eames Lounge Chair, Barcelona chair, Wassily chair, Panton chair, Tulip table, Egg and Swan chairs, Wishbone chair, Bertoia wire chairs, Tolix metal chairs, Arco and PH5 lamps, and Noguchi coffee table.
Buying a copy knowingly at a copy price is your choice. The problem is paying for an original and getting a replica, which is hard to undo once you have paid cash and driven home.

faq.q: How do I know if a designer chair is original?
faq.a: Check the maker's label or stamp, ask for the original receipt, and compare proportions and materials with the official product. A price far below the usual used price is a strong warning.

faq.q: Are replicas always cheap?
faq.a: Mostly, but some sellers ask near original prices for good copies. That is why labels and receipts matter more than the price alone.

faq.q: What does in de stijl van mean in a listing?
faq.a: It means in the style of. It is a polite way of saying the item is not the original design.

faq.q: What can I do if I bought a replica sold as original?
faq.a: Contact the seller first with your evidence. If that fails, you can report the listing to Marktplaats, and for larger amounts consider getting legal advice.

example_wish: Original Knoll or Vitra designer lounge chair with label or receipt, no replica or style copies, under 1500 euro, anywhere in the Netherlands

title: Flipping vintage furniture from Marktplaats: a realistic guide
meta_title: Flipping vintage furniture from Marktplaats
description: A realistic guide to flipping vintage furniture from Marktplaats: what sells, what to skip, true costs of transport and restoring, and tax reporting.
intro: Flipping vintage furniture can pay, but most of the money is made when you buy, not when you sell. You need cheap good pieces, a way to move them, space to store them and patience, and you have to count your hours honestly. Here is what works in the Netherlands and what tends to sit unsold for months.

sections.heading: What sells and what does not
paragraphs: Demand is strong for mid-century teak and oak sideboards of moderate size, sets of design dining chairs, vintage lamps, rattan pieces, small cabinets and known Dutch and Danish makers. These fit in modern apartments and look good in photos.

Slow sellers are big dark oak cabinets (eiken kasten), heavy wall units, wardrobes, 1990s glass and chrome, and anything over two metres that needs three people to carry. You will see these offered free constantly. Free is not a bargain if nobody wants to buy it from you either.

sections.heading: Count every cost
paragraphs: Do the sum before you message the seller. A sideboard bought for EUR 150 and sold for EUR 450 sounds like EUR 300 profit, but that is before the rest.
bullets: Transport twice: picking up and often delivering, a rented van or fuel and your time
Materials: sandpaper, oil, veneer glue, new knobs, upholstery fabric, foam
Specialist work you cannot do yourself, such as cord seats, rechroming or veneer repair
Storage: a shed, garage or rented unit, plus the risk of damp
Paid listing options if you use them to push a slow item
Your hours, including messages from buyers who never turn up

sections.heading: Buying well
paragraphs: Search in Dutch and by description, not only by brand. Listings like oude kast van oma, dressoir teak opknapper or stoelen zolder are where unrecognised pieces sit. Check new listings several times a day for the categories you know, because dealers do the same. A plain-language search on vindje.com can watch for things like a teak sideboard under EUR 200 within 30 km in good structural condition, so you are not paging through hundreds of results.
Only buy what you can identify and value. A good flipper knows the difference between a Pastoe cabinet and a look-alike from across the room. If you are unsure, pass.

sections.heading: Restore with a light hand
paragraphs: Clean first. Many pieces look transformed after a wash with mild soap, a light rub with fine steel wool and a coat of oil. Fix loose joints and sticking drawers. Avoid stripping and varnishing original finishes on design pieces; buyers pay for original condition.
Do not hide damage. Photograph repairs and mention them. Buyers on Marktplaats compare photos with what they see at pickup, and a bad surprise ends the sale and leads to a bad review.

sections.heading: Selling: photos, price and patience
paragraphs: Take photos in daylight against a plain wall, include the label, the back, inside drawers and any damage, and give exact dimensions. Name the maker only if you can show proof.

Price a little above what you will accept, because almost every buyer asks for a discount. Watch how quickly similar listings disappear to judge demand; listings that stay up for weeks at a certain price tell you that price is too high.

sections.heading: Tax and registration
paragraphs: Selling your own used things now and then is normal. Buying to resell regularly with a profit motive can count as business activity for the Belastingdienst, which may mean registering with the KVK and declaring income. Under the EU's DAC7 rules, platforms report sellers above certain thresholds of sales or turnover to the tax office. If you plan to flip regularly, check your situation with the Belastingdienst or an adviser first.

price_guide.item: Teak sideboard: sell cleaned and oiled
Set of 4 vintage dining chairs: buy
Set of 4 vintage dining chairs: sell restored
Van rental for one day, local

faq.q: Is flipping furniture profitable in the Netherlands?
faq.a: It can be for small, popular vintage pieces bought cheaply. Once you count transport, materials, storage and your time, the margin on most items is smaller than it looks.

faq.q: What vintage furniture sells best on Marktplaats?
faq.a: Mid-century teak sideboards, design dining chairs, vintage lamps, rattan and pieces by known makers sell best. Large dark wood cabinets and wardrobes sell slowly.

faq.q: Do I need to pay tax on furniture I resell?
faq.a: Occasional sales of your own items are generally not a business. Regular buying to resell for profit can be, so check with the Belastingdienst if you do this often.

faq.q: Should I refinish vintage furniture before selling?
faq.a: Clean and oil it and fix structural problems, but avoid stripping original finishes on design pieces. Buyers usually prefer original condition.

example_wish: Teak or oak sideboard from the 1960s, solid structure, veneer may need work, max 160 cm wide, under 200 euro, within 30 km of Eindhoven

title: Buying vintage rattan and wicker furniture
meta_title: Buying vintage rattan and wicker furniture
description: How to buy vintage rattan and wicker furniture second hand: rotan versus pitriet, Rohé Noordwolde, checks for brittle strands and woodworm, and prices.
intro: Vintage rattan is back in demand, and the Netherlands has plenty of it, including pieces by the Noordwolde factories. Good rattan lasts decades if it has been kept indoors. Check for brittle, snapping strands, loose joints and woodworm, and know that painted rattan often hides repairs.

sections.heading: Rattan, wicker and the Dutch words
paragraphs: Rattan (rotan) is a climbing palm with solid, strong stems used for frames. Wicker describes the weaving, which can be done with rattan core (pitriet), willow (wilgentenen), reed (riet) or seagrass. Dutch sellers mix these words, so search rotan, pitriet and riet.

Peacock chairs with a tall fan back are pauwenstoel. Bamboo pieces (bamboe) look similar but are hollow and lighter. Modern garden sets are often poly rattan, a plastic weave, which is a different product altogether.

sections.heading: Dutch makers to look for
paragraphs: Noordwolde in Friesland was the centre of Dutch rattan and wicker furniture. Rohé Noordwolde made well known mid-century designs, many by Dirk van Sliedregt, and Gebroeders Jonker also worked there. Their chairs, lounge chairs and side tables are wanted by collectors and decorators.
Labels are often missing, so compare shapes and construction with documented pieces. Many listings say Rohé for anything with a bent rattan frame; ask what the claim is based on.

sections.heading: Inspection checklist
paragraphs: Rattan problems are easy to see if you take a few minutes.
bullets: Run your hand over the weave: brittle strands snap, frayed ends stick out
Check the bindings at joints, where frame parts are wrapped: they should be tight, not unravelling
Sit down and rock gently: creaks are normal, a frame that shifts is not
Look for tiny round holes with fine powder underneath, a sign of woodworm
Smell and look for dark spots from mould, common after storage in a shed
Look at the underside and back of painted pieces for patched or replaced sections

sections.heading: Cleaning and care
paragraphs: Vacuum with a brush nozzle to get dust out of the weave, then wipe with a cloth and mild soapy water. Do not soak it. Dry it quickly in a warm, airy place but out of strong sun. Rattan that feels dry and stiff can be misted lightly with water and left to dry; it becomes a little more flexible.

Keep vintage rattan indoors. Rain, frost and sun break it down quickly, and most old pieces were never meant for outdoor use. If you have woodworm, treat it before the piece goes near other wooden furniture.

sections.heading: Repairs and value
paragraphs: Small breaks in the weave can be repaired by a specialist rattan or chair weaver, and replacing a woven seat is common. Broken frame parts are harder. Price a chair with a cracked frame member as a project.

If you are after a specific shape, such as a low lounge chair with a bent rattan frame and woven seat from the 1960s, vindje.com can search on that description and include listings titled only oude stoel.

sections.heading: Timing, transport and what to skip
paragraphs: Rattan is light, so most chairs fit in a small car or even on a cargo bike, which widens the area you can buy from. Prices tend to climb in spring when people think about balconies and conservatories, and more people clear out sheds in autumn, so autumn and winter are often a better time to buy.

Skip pieces that have stood outside for years: grey, splintering strands and a soft frame mean the material is finished. Also be careful with cheap import chairs from the 2000s sold as vintage. They are often stapled rather than bound at the joints and break quickly. A flimsy feel when you lift it is the giveaway.

price_guide.item: Pitriet basket chair or small side table

faq.q: What is the difference between rattan and wicker?
faq.a: Rattan is a material, a palm stem. Wicker is a weaving technique that can use rattan, willow, reed or other fibres.

faq.q: Can I use vintage rattan furniture outside?
faq.a: Not long term. Natural rattan weakens with rain, frost and sun, so keep it indoors or in a covered spot and bring it in for winter.

faq.q: How do I recognise Rohé Noordwolde furniture?
faq.a: Look for a label and compare the design with documented Rohé pieces, many designed by Dirk van Sliedregt. Without a label, treat the attribution as uncertain.

faq.q: Can broken rattan be repaired?
faq.a: Breaks in the woven parts and seats can usually be repaired by a specialist. A broken main frame is a bigger job.

example_wish: Vintage rattan lounge chair from the 1960s, Rohé Noordwolde or similar, no broken strands or woodworm, under 250 euro, within 50 km

title: West German pottery (fat lava) and vintage ceramics second hand
meta_title: West German pottery and fat lava vases second hand
description: Buying West German pottery and fat lava vases second hand: makers like Scheurich and Ruscha, reading base marks, spotting damage and fair prices.
intro: West German pottery from the 1950s to the 1970s is common on Marktplaats, often at EUR 5-30 a piece. Most of it is decorative rather than valuable, but certain makers, shapes and thick lava glazes are collected seriously. The base mark and a careful look for chips tell you most of what you need.

sections.heading: What fat lava means
paragraphs: Fat lava is a collectors' name for West German ceramics with thick, bubbly, cratered glazes, usually in bold colours like orange, red, brown and black. It sits within the wider category of West German pottery, which also includes smoother drip glazes, matt finishes and decorated vases.
Dutch sellers use West Germany, W. Germany, fat lava and vintage vaas. Many just write oude vaas and show the base in a photo, so check every picture.

sections.heading: Makers to recognise
paragraphs: Dozens of factories produced this work. These names come up most often.
bullets: Scheurich: the most common, many shapes, from cheap to collectible depending on glaze
Ruscha: known for clean shapes and some designs by well known names
Bay Keramik: vases and bowls, including glazes that collectors look for
Carstens, Jopeko, Dümler & Breiden, ES Keramik, Roth, Otto Keramik and Fohr
Studio potters and smaller workshops, often with a signature or monogram rather than a printed mark

sections.heading: Reading the base
paragraphs: Most pieces are marked W. Germany or West Germany on the base, followed by numbers. The number is usually a shape code and the height in centimetres, separated by a dash or slash, like 414-16. Some factories add their name or a logo, many do not.

Collectors identify unmarked pieces by shape number style, clay colour on the unglazed base and glaze. A W. Germany mark only tells you the country and era (after 1949 and before reunification), not that the piece is valuable.

sections.heading: Checking condition
paragraphs: Damage cuts value sharply, so inspect each piece in good light.
bullets: Run a fingertip slowly around the rim and base for chips and flea bites
Look inside the neck, where cracks hide
Tap gently with a fingernail: a clear ring is good, a dull sound can mean a crack
Look for areas where the glaze shine is different, a sign of restoration
Check the handles, the most fragile part on many shapes

sections.heading: What is worth more
paragraphs: Large floor vases, unusual shapes, and strong lava glazes in colour combinations collectors like fetch the higher prices. Small, common shapes in brown drip glaze are the everyday end and rarely go above EUR 20-30.

Other vintage ceramics are worth knowing too: Dutch makers like Mobach, Fris Edam and Zaalberg, Danish studio ceramics, and German porcelain like Rosenthal studio line. If you are searching broadly, describing the piece on vindje.com, for example a large orange fat lava floor vase with no chips, catches listings that never use the term fat lava.

sections.heading: Buying and shipping
paragraphs: Mixed lots (partij keramiek, verzameling vazen) from house clearances are where the cheap finds are, often priced by the box. Ask for a photo of every base before you go.

If a seller offers to post a vase, ask how it will be packed: double boxed, wrapped, with no movement inside. A broken vase sent by post is hard to claim back, so collecting in person is safer for anything you value.

sections.heading: Cleaning and display
paragraphs: Wash glazed pieces by hand in lukewarm water with a little washing-up liquid and a soft brush for the craters of lava glazes. Never put them in the dishwasher. Many of these vases were made for dried flowers and are not fully watertight, so test with water in a sink before using one for fresh flowers, or put a glass insert inside.

Groups look better than single pieces: three or five vases in one colour family on a sideboard is how most collectors display them, and buying matching colours in one lot is often cheaper than collecting them one by one.

price_guide.item: Small West German vase, common glaze
Medium fat lava vase, good glaze
Large floor vase, 40 cm and up
Sought after shape or glaze from a known maker

faq.q: What does W. Germany on the bottom of a vase mean?
faq.a: It means the piece was made in West Germany, between 1949 and 1990. The numbers after it are usually the shape code and height in centimetres.

faq.q: Is West German pottery valuable?
faq.a: Most pieces are worth EUR 5-50. Large vases, rare shapes and well known glazes from certain makers can be worth more, especially in perfect condition.

faq.q: How do I identify an unmarked West German vase?
faq.a: Compare the shape number, clay colour and glaze with collector references and online archives. Collector groups often help identify pieces from photos.

faq.q: Does a chip ruin the value?
faq.a: It lowers it a lot. A small chip on the base matters less than one on the rim or a crack running into the body.

example_wish: Large West German fat lava floor vase, at least 40 cm, orange or red lava glaze, no chips, under 120 euro, within 40 km

title: Old IKEA designs that became collectible
meta_title: Collectible old IKEA furniture: what to look for
description: Which old IKEA designs became collectible: pieces by known designers, limited collaborations, how to check labels, and realistic second-hand prices.
intro: Most used IKEA furniture is worth little, but a handful of older designs and limited collaborations now sell for more than they cost new. They are usually pieces with a known designer, a short production run or a strong style. A label under the furniture is the easiest way to confirm what you have.

sections.heading: Why some IKEA became collectible
paragraphs: IKEA has worked with well known designers for decades, and some designs were only made for a few years. When a style becomes popular again, those pieces get noticed. Collectors look for bold postmodern shapes from the 1980s and 1990s, early versions of designs that are still sold in changed form, and limited editions.
None of this applies to Billy bookcases, Kallax shelves or the Lack table. Those are everywhere and priced like ordinary furniture, however old they are.

sections.heading: Pieces to look out for
paragraphs: These are among the older designs that collectors and stylists search for.
bullets: Vilbert: a flat-pack chair made of four panels, designed by Verner Panton in the 1990s
Moment: the chrome and lacquer sofa and table series by Niels Gammelgaard from the 1980s
Poem: the original 1970s version of the chair later sold as Poäng, designed by Noboru Nakamura
Early bentwood and cantilever chairs from the 1970s and 1980s, often in chrome tube
Lövet table by Gillis Lundgren, IKEA's first flat-pack table, later reissued
Old PS collection pieces, IKEA's design-led series that started in the 1990s

sections.heading: Limited collaborations
paragraphs: IKEA has released limited collections with outside designers and brands, such as the Markerad collection with Virgil Abloh and collaborations with HAY and others. Some pieces, especially rugs and objects with strong graphics, resell above their original price.
Resale value is unpredictable and can fall as quickly as it rose. Buy collaboration pieces because you like them, and be wary of paying a premium for items that were made in large numbers.

sections.heading: Checking labels and age
paragraphs: Most IKEA furniture has a sticker, stamp or printed label with the IKEA name and the model name, often with a production date or code. Older labels can include the designer's name. Ask the seller for a photo of it.

IKEA has also reissued older designs, for example in its Nytillverkad collection. A reissue is a good piece of furniture but not a vintage original, and the label usually shows a recent year. Price it accordingly.

sections.heading: Condition and completeness
paragraphs: Flat-pack furniture that has been taken apart several times can have worn screw holes and missing fittings. Check that the original connectors and screws are present, as replacements for old models are rarely available. On upholstered pieces, original covers add value; on Poem chairs the original fabric is part of what collectors want.
Chrome on 1980s pieces should be checked for rust and pitting, and lacquered surfaces for chips, which are hard to repair invisibly.

sections.heading: Finding them
paragraphs: Sellers often list these as old IKEA chair without the model name, or do not know the item is IKEA at all. Searching by description helps: a plain-language search on vindje.com for a 1990s flat-pack plywood chair, or a chrome and black lacquer sofa from the 1980s, can surface listings that never mention Vilbert or Moment.

sections.heading: Buying to resell
paragraphs: Some people buy old IKEA cheaply to resell it to collectors abroad, where some of these pieces fetch more. Be realistic: shipping a chair is expensive, the collector market is small, and prices are driven by trends. Check how many of the same item are listed and for how long before you buy several.
For your own home, the appeal is simpler. A Vilbert chair or a Moment table is a good design piece at a fraction of the price of comparable furniture from the big design brands.

price_guide.item: Ordinary used IKEA chair or table

faq.q: Is old IKEA furniture worth money?
faq.a: Most of it is not. A few designs by known designers, short production runs and limited collaborations do sell for more than ordinary used furniture.

faq.q: How can I tell how old my IKEA furniture is?
faq.a: Look for a label or stamp underneath or on the back. It usually shows the model name and often a production date or code.

faq.q: What was the Poäng chair originally called?
faq.a: It was launched in the 1970s as Poem, designed by Noboru Nakamura, and renamed Poäng later.

faq.q: Are IKEA reissues collectible?
faq.a: Reissued designs are good furniture but are worth less to collectors than original production pieces.

example_wish: IKEA Vilbert chair by Verner Panton, original 1990s, all panels intact, under 200 euro, anywhere in the Netherlands

title: How to buy a used iPhone without getting scammed
meta_title: Buy a used iPhone without getting scammed
description: How to buy a used iPhone on Marktplaats safely: Activation Lock, battery health, parts history, fake iPhones, payment scams and fair prices in 2026.
intro: A used iPhone can be a great deal, but it is also the most scammed category on Marktplaats. Never buy one that is still linked to someone's Apple account, check the battery and parts history in Settings, and only pay in person once you have tested it. The checks take ten minutes.

sections.heading: The scams that come up most
paragraphs: Most bad iPhone deals fall into a few patterns. The price is the first clue: a recent Pro model listed at half the usual used price is bait.
bullets: Sellers who will only ship and want payment first, often with a story about living far away
Payment links or verification requests sent by chat, which lead to a fake bank page
iCloud-locked phones sold as normal, or as for parts at a price that suggests they work
Clone phones running Android in an iPhone-like case, sold sealed or in a copied box
Company phones under device management (MDM) that the employer can lock remotely
Phones swapped after testing: keep the phone you tested in your hand until you pay

sections.heading: Activation Lock: the one check you cannot skip
paragraphs: If Find My (Zoek mijn) is still on, the phone is tied to the seller's Apple account. After a reset it will ask for their Apple ID and password, and without them it is useless. Apple will not remove it for you without proof of purchase.

Ask the seller to sign out of their Apple account in Settings, then erase the phone in front of you (Settings, General, Transfer or Reset iPhone, Erase All Content and Settings). When it restarts on the Hello screen and lets you go through setup without asking for someone else's Apple ID, it is clean. If the seller cannot or will not do this, do not buy it.

sections.heading: Battery and parts history
paragraphs: Go to Settings, Battery, Battery Health. Below 80 percent maximum capacity, the battery is due for replacement, which Apple and repair shops charge for. Recent models also show the cycle count under Settings, General, About.

In Settings, General, About you will also find Parts and Service History on supported models. It shows whether the screen, battery or camera were replaced and whether the part is genuine Apple or Unknown Part. A cheap aftermarket screen can have worse colours and touch response, and lowers the value.

sections.heading: Test everything in person
paragraphs: Bring your own SIM card and a cable, and work through the phone in order.
bullets: Put your SIM in and make a call, check both the earpiece and the speaker
Set up Face ID or Touch ID during setup to confirm it works
Open the camera, try every lens and the front camera, and record a short video
Plug in to charge and check the port is not loose
Check Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and the buttons, including the mute switch or action button
Dial *#06# and check the IMEI matches the box and the Settings screen
Look at the screen on a white background for dead pixels and burn-in

sections.heading: Models and storage in 2026
paragraphs: An iPhone 13 or newer is a sensible minimum this year if you want several more years of updates. The iPhone 15 and later use USB-C, which matters if you want to share chargers with other devices. Go for at least 128 GB; 64 GB fills up quickly with photos.

Note that iPhones from the US since the iPhone 14 have no SIM tray and work with eSIM only. Check that your Dutch provider supports eSIM before buying an imported phone. If you want a narrow match, for example an iPhone 15 Pro with battery health over 85 percent and no replaced parts within 20 km, vindje.com can check listing descriptions for those details.

faq.q: How do I check if a used iPhone is iCloud locked?
faq.a: Ask the seller to erase it in front of you. If it starts setup without asking for another person's Apple ID, Activation Lock is off.

faq.q: What battery health is acceptable on a used iPhone?
faq.a: Above 85 percent is good. Below 80 percent you should plan on a battery replacement and lower your offer.

faq.q: Is it safe to buy an iPhone that is shipped?
faq.a: It is riskier, because you cannot check Activation Lock or test it before paying. If you must, only use a payment method with buyer protection.

faq.q: How can I spot a fake iPhone?
faq.a: Check Settings, General, About for the model and serial number, and enter the serial on Apple's coverage check site. Clones often have Android-style menus, no App Store and a wrong About screen.

example_wish: iPhone 15 or 15 Pro, at least 128 GB, battery health above 85 percent, no replaced parts, pickup only, under 550 euro, within 20 km

title: Buying a used MacBook: which models, what to check
meta_title: Buying a used MacBook: models and checks
description: Which used MacBook to buy in 2026 and what to check: Apple Silicon versus Intel, RAM, battery cycles, Activation Lock, company management and fair prices.
intro: For most people the best used MacBook in 2026 is an Apple Silicon model: a MacBook Air M1 or M2 for everyday use, a 14 inch MacBook Pro for heavier work. Skip Intel MacBooks unless they are very cheap. Before paying, check Activation Lock, company management, battery cycles and the keyboard layout.

sections.heading: Apple Silicon or Intel
paragraphs: Since late 2020 MacBooks use Apple's own chips (M1, M2, M3, M4 and later). They are faster, cooler, quieter and have much better battery life than the Intel models before them. Apple has said that macOS 26 is the last version for Intel Macs, so an Intel MacBook will stop getting new macOS versions.

Intel MacBook Pros from 2016 to 2019 also had the butterfly keyboard, which is known for sticking keys, and a Touch Bar that some people find annoying. If you see one at a low price, treat it as a basic machine with limited life.

sections.heading: Which model fits you
paragraphs: MacBook Air M1: still a very good machine for browsing, writing, study and photo editing, and the cheapest way into Apple Silicon. MacBook Air M2 and later: thinner design, larger screen, MagSafe charging. 14 inch MacBook Pro with M1 Pro or newer: better screen, more ports, sustained performance for video, code and music.
Memory cannot be upgraded later. 8 GB works for light use, but 16 GB makes the machine last longer. Storage also cannot be upgraded; 256 GB is tight if you keep photos locally.

sections.heading: Activation Lock and company management
paragraphs: Like an iPhone, a Mac with Find My on is locked to the owner's Apple account. Ask the seller to sign out of their Apple account and erase the Mac in front of you (System Settings, General, Transfer or Reset, Erase All Content and Settings). It should restart to the setup screen without asking for another person's Apple ID.

Company laptops are a second risk. If during setup you see a Remote Management screen naming an organisation, the Mac is enrolled in device management and the company can control or lock it. Do not buy it unless the seller can show it has been released.

sections.heading: Checks at the pickup
paragraphs: Bring a USB stick or phone with a few files and some headphones.
bullets: Open Apple menu, About This Mac, and confirm chip, memory and storage match the ad
In System Information, Power, read the cycle count and condition; under about 300 cycles is light use
Type on every key and test the trackpad click in all corners
Check the screen on white and black backgrounds for marks, dead pixels and pressure spots
Test speakers, webcam, microphone, Wi-Fi and every port
Plug in the charger and confirm it charges; ask for the original adapter
Look at the corners and lid for dents, which can affect the screen

sections.heading: Keyboard layout and imports
paragraphs: Most MacBooks sold in the Netherlands have a US English style layout, which is what most Dutch users want. Imported machines can have German QWERTZ, Belgian or French AZERTY, or UK layouts. Check the photos or ask, especially when the price is low.

If you know exactly what you want, such as a MacBook Air M2 with 16 GB, under 150 battery cycles and a US layout within 30 km, vindje.com can filter on those details in the description rather than only the model name.

faq.q: Is a used MacBook Air M1 still worth it in 2026?
faq.a: Yes, for everyday use it is still fast and well supported. Aim for good battery condition and pay less for 8 GB models.

faq.q: How many battery cycles is too many for a MacBook?
faq.a: Apple rates recent MacBook batteries for around 1000 cycles. Above about 700, or with a Service Recommended status, budget for a replacement.

faq.q: How do I check if a MacBook is locked?
faq.a: Have the seller sign out of their Apple account and erase the Mac. If setup starts without asking for someone else's Apple ID or showing Remote Management, it is clear.

faq.q: Can I upgrade the memory or SSD in a used MacBook?
faq.a: No. On Apple Silicon MacBooks the memory and storage are part of the main board, so buy the configuration you need from the start. External SSDs are a cheap way to add storage for files.

faq.q: Should I buy an Intel MacBook?
faq.a: Only if it is cheap and for light use. Intel Macs no longer get new macOS versions after macOS 26 and are slower and hotter than Apple Silicon models.

example_wish: MacBook Air M2 or M3 with 16 GB RAM and 512 GB, battery under 200 cycles, US keyboard, no company management, under 800 euro, within 30 km

title: Buying a used Windows laptop: specs that matter
meta_title: Used Windows laptop: which specs matter
description: How to buy a used Windows laptop in the Netherlands: CPU, RAM and SSD minimums, Windows 11 support, ex-business ThinkPads, company locks and fair prices.
intro: A good used Windows laptop in 2026 has a processor that runs Windows 11, at least 16 GB of RAM, an SSD and a 1080p IPS screen. Former business laptops like ThinkPads, Latitudes and EliteBooks are often better buys than consumer models at the same price. Check the battery and make sure it is not locked to a company.

sections.heading: Windows 11 support comes first
paragraphs: Free support for Windows 10 ended in October 2025, so you want a laptop that officially supports Windows 11. In practice that means an Intel Core processor from the 8th generation onward or an AMD Ryzen 2000 series or newer, plus TPM 2.0, which almost all such laptops have.

You can find the processor in Settings, System, About, or in the listing. An Intel i5-8250U is 8th generation; an i7-7700HQ is 7th and not supported. Older laptops can still run Linux well, but price them as such.

sections.heading: Specs that make the difference
paragraphs: Processor names are confusing, but a few rules cover most of it.
bullets: RAM: 16 GB is the comfortable minimum now; check whether it can be upgraded, many thin laptops have it soldered
Storage: an SSD, ideally NVMe, of at least 256 GB; never buy a laptop with only a spinning hard drive as the main disk
Screen: 1920x1080 IPS; avoid 1366x768 and TN panels, which look washed out from an angle
Processor: Intel Core i5 or Ryzen 5 of a recent generation is plenty for office work and study
Ports: USB-C charging is handy, and HDMI saves buying adapters
Weight: under 1.5 kg if you carry it daily

sections.heading: Why ex-business laptops are a good deal
paragraphs: Companies lease laptops for three or four years and then sell them in bulk. Lenovo ThinkPad T and X series, Dell Latitude 5000 and 7000 series and HP EliteBook 800 series are built to last, have good keyboards, and parts like batteries and keyboards are easy to buy. Many are sold on Marktplaats by refurbishers with a short warranty.
Consumer laptops at the same age are often thinner and prettier but have weaker hinges, cheaper screens and fewer spare parts.

sections.heading: Company locks and passwords
paragraphs: Laptops from companies can still be tied to their management. If, after a reset, Windows asks you to sign in with a work account or shows the company's name, it is enrolled in Windows Autopilot or similar and you will not get past it. Also ask whether there is a BIOS password; a locked BIOS can block resets and upgrades.

The safe way to test: ask the seller to reset Windows before the meeting, then go through the setup yourself on the spot. A laptop that reaches the normal Windows welcome screen and lets you create a local or personal account is clean.

sections.heading: Pickup tests
paragraphs: Run through these in ten minutes, with the charger unplugged for part of the time.
bullets: Open Command Prompt and run powercfg /batteryreport, then compare full charge capacity with design capacity
Check Task Manager, Performance, for the installed processor, RAM and disk
Type on every key, test the touchpad and both buttons
Open and close the lid several times, the hinges should be firm with no cracking
Play a video for sound and look at the screen on white for dead pixels
Test every USB port, the headphone jack, Wi-Fi and the webcam
Make sure the charger is the right wattage, not a weaker generic one

sections.heading: Search tips
paragraphs: Search by model as well as by laptop: ThinkPad T14, Latitude 5420, EliteBook 840 G8. The model number tells you more than the brand. On vindje.com you can describe what you need, like a business laptop with 16 GB, a 1080p screen and Windows 11 under EUR 350, and the AI checks the specs in each description.

price_guide.item: ThinkPad T14 Gen 2 or EliteBook 840 G8
Consumer laptop, 3-4 years old, i5 or Ryzen 5

faq.q: How much RAM should a used laptop have?
faq.a: 16 GB is the comfortable minimum in 2026. 8 GB works for light browsing and documents but feels slow with many browser tabs.

faq.q: Will my used laptop run Windows 11?
faq.a: Officially, if it has an 8th generation Intel Core or Ryzen 2000 processor or newer, plus TPM 2.0. Check the processor in Settings or Task Manager.

faq.q: Are refurbished ThinkPads worth it?
faq.a: Usually yes. They are built for business use, easy to repair, and good value three or four years after they were new.

faq.q: How do I check laptop battery health on Windows?
faq.a: Run powercfg /batteryreport in Command Prompt and open the report. Compare full charge capacity with design capacity; under about 70 percent means short battery life.

example_wish: Business laptop like a ThinkPad T14 or Dell Latitude, 16 GB RAM, SSD, 1080p IPS screen, runs Windows 11, battery over 80 percent, under 350 euro

title: Buying a used iPad: models, iCloud lock and battery
meta_title: Buying a used iPad: models, iCloud lock, battery
description: How to buy a used iPad safely: which models still make sense in 2026, avoiding iCloud and school-locked iPads, battery checks, Pencil support and prices.
intro: Used iPads are easy to find and good value, but a large share of the cheap ones are iCloud locked or managed by a school or company. Make sure it is reset and free of Activation Lock in front of you, check that the model still gets updates, and match it to the Apple Pencil you want to use.

sections.heading: Which iPads still make sense
paragraphs: Every iPad looks similar in photos, so read the model number (Settings, General, About). In 2026 a sensible minimum for most people is the 9th generation iPad, which still has a home button and Lightning port and is very cheap. The 10th generation and later standard iPads have USB-C and a modern design.

The iPad Air with M1 or newer and the iPad Pro with an M-series chip are the ones to buy for drawing, multitasking or using a keyboard as a laptop replacement. The iPad mini is the choice for reading and carrying in a jacket pocket.

sections.heading: Activation Lock and managed iPads
paragraphs: An iPad still linked to someone's Apple account becomes a brick after a reset. Cheap iPads sold without a charger, without the box and with vague stories are often lost or stolen, or locked by a forgotten password. Ask the seller to sign out and erase it in front of you, and only pay once you see the Hello screen and can start setup without another person's Apple ID.

Dutch schools hand out many iPads, and companies use them too. These are enrolled in device management. During setup a Remote Management screen naming a school or company means the organisation still controls it. Those iPads are not yours to use, even if the seller says the school no longer needs it.

sections.heading: Battery and screen
paragraphs: iPad batteries last a long time but wear out like any other. Recent iPads show battery health and cycle count under Settings, Battery; on older models you can check it with a Mac and a third-party tool, or judge it by how quickly the percentage drops while you test.

Look at the screen on a white background for yellow patches, pressure marks and dead pixels. Check that the iPad lies flat on a table: some thin iPad Pro models can bend, and a bent iPad can crack later.

sections.heading: Apple Pencil and keyboard compatibility
paragraphs: Apple has several Pencils, and each iPad works with only some of them. The first generation Pencil works with older iPads like the 9th generation. The second generation Pencil works with iPad Air 4 and later and recent Pro and mini models. Newer USB-C and Pro Pencils fit the most recent models. Check Apple's compatibility list before buying an iPad and Pencil separately.
Keyboard cases are model specific too. A Magic Keyboard for one iPad Pro generation may not fit the next.

sections.heading: Test at the pickup
paragraphs: Bring a cable and, for cellular models, your SIM card.
bullets: Erase and start setup to confirm no Activation Lock or Remote Management
Check Settings, General, About for model and storage
Test Touch ID or Face ID, both cameras, speakers and microphone
Charge it and check the port is not loose
If it includes a Pencil, pair it and draw across the whole screen
Check Wi-Fi and, on cellular models, mobile data with your SIM

sections.heading: Storage and models to skip
paragraphs: 32 GB iPads are hard to live with now; 64 GB is the practical minimum, 128 GB or more if you download films for travel. Skip iPads from before the 9th generation and the first iPad Air and mini models. They are stuck on old iPadOS versions and many apps no longer support them.

If you need a specific setup, such as an iPad Air with M1 and a second generation Pencil, at least 64 GB, within 15 km, vindje.com can read the descriptions for those details instead of matching only the word iPad.

faq.q: How do I check if a used iPad is iCloud locked?
faq.a: Have the seller erase it in front of you. If setup starts without asking for another person's Apple ID, it is free of Activation Lock.

faq.q: Can Activation Lock on a used iPad be removed?
faq.a: Only by the original owner, or by Apple with proof of purchase. Paid removal services advertised online are unreliable or scams.

faq.q: Which used iPad is best for drawing?
faq.a: An iPad Air with M1 or newer, or an iPad Pro, with a second generation or newer Apple Pencil. The smooth Pencil support and laminated screen make a big difference.

faq.q: Is a school iPad safe to buy?
faq.a: Not if it shows Remote Management during setup. It belongs to the school's management system and can be locked or wiped by them.

example_wish: iPad Air M1 or newer, at least 64 GB, with second generation Apple Pencil, no iCloud lock or school management, under 400 euro, within 15 km

title: Buying a used gaming PC: what to test before paying
meta_title: Buying a used gaming PC: what to test
description: What to test before paying for a used gaming PC: verify the GPU and CPU, run a stress test, check temperatures, the power supply and fair 2026 prices.
intro: A used gaming PC can save you hundreds of euro, but sellers sometimes list better parts than are inside, and some machines run hot or crash under load. Ask to see it running, verify each component in software, run a stress test for at least 15 minutes and look inside the case before you hand over money.

sections.heading: Before you go
paragraphs: Ask the seller for the exact parts list: processor, graphics card model, motherboard, RAM amount and speed, storage, power supply brand and wattage, and case. Look the parts up to check the price makes sense. A listing that says RTX graphics without a model, or i7 without a generation, is too vague.

Ask whether the PC can be tested on arrival with a monitor, keyboard and mouse. A seller who refuses a test or wants to meet in a car park with a PC you cannot plug in is a reason to walk away. Bring a USB stick with portable tools such as CPU-Z, GPU-Z and HWiNFO.

sections.heading: Verify the parts in software
paragraphs: Open Task Manager, Performance, to see the processor, RAM and GPU. Then run CPU-Z for the CPU, motherboard and memory, and GPU-Z for the graphics card. GPU-Z also shows memory size and whether the card's details match the model name.
Compare everything with the parts list. Common tricks are an RTX 3060 sold as a 3070, 8 GB of RAM where 16 was promised, or a small SSD with a big slow hard drive listed as total storage.

sections.heading: The stress test
paragraphs: Idle PCs rarely show problems. Put load on it while you watch temperatures in HWiNFO.
bullets: Run a GPU benchmark like Unigine Superposition or 3DMark for 10-15 minutes
Run Cinebench or a similar CPU test for a few minutes
GPU temperatures under about 85 degrees and CPU under about 90 degrees under full load are normal for most parts
Watch for crashes, black screens, artefacts (coloured blocks, flicker) or a sudden shutdown
Listen for a coil whine or grinding fan, and for fans running at full speed all the time
If possible, play a demanding game for a few minutes at the settings you plan to use

sections.heading: Look inside the case
paragraphs: With the power off, open the side panel. Heavy dust means poor maintenance and probably higher temperatures. Look at the power supply label: a known brand with an 80 Plus rating and enough wattage for the GPU matters, because a cheap unbranded PSU is the part most likely to fail and take other parts with it.

Check that the graphics card is properly supported and not sagging badly, cables are connected firmly, and there are no burn marks on the GPU power connector. That last point matters especially on high end cards with the newer 12-pin style connector.

sections.heading: Former mining cards and Windows
paragraphs: Graphics cards used for cryptocurrency mining are not automatically bad, since many were run undervolted in steady conditions, but fans and thermal pads may be worn. Ask directly how the PC was used and price in fan replacement if the card is loud.

Check whether Windows is activated (Settings, System, Activation). An unactivated copy means you will need to buy a licence. Ask the seller to reset Windows or plan to do a clean install yourself, since you do not know what software was installed.

sections.heading: Matching it to your monitor
paragraphs: Buy for the resolution you play at. A PC with an RTX 4060 or RX 7600 is good for 1080p, an RTX 4070 class card handles 1440p, and 4K needs much more. If you are browsing many listings, vindje.com can filter on details like an RTX 4070 or better, at least 32 GB RAM and a known brand power supply within 30 km, which saves opening every ad.

price_guide.item: Entry PC: GTX 1660 or RX 6600, Ryzen 5 3600
RTX 3070, 4060 Ti or RX 6700 XT build

faq.q: How do I check what graphics card is in a used PC?
faq.a: Open Task Manager, Performance, or run GPU-Z. Both show the exact card and memory size, which you can compare with the listing.

faq.q: What temperature is too hot for a gaming PC?
faq.a: Under full load, most GPUs should stay below about 85 degrees and most CPUs below about 90. Higher than that, or crashes during a stress test, point to cooling problems.

faq.q: Is it safe to buy a used graphics card that was used for mining?
faq.a: Often it is fine, but fans and thermal pads may be worn. Test it under load and expect to replace fans on a noisy card.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to buy a used gaming PC or build one?
faq.a: A complete used PC is often cheaper than the parts separately, especially with an older generation GPU. Building gives you more control and new warranties.

example_wish: Gaming PC with RTX 4070 or better, Ryzen 7 or i7, 32 GB RAM, 1 TB SSD, branded power supply, seller lets me test it, under 1300 euro, within 30 km

title: Buying a used PlayStation 5: models, prices and what to test
meta_title: Buying a used PS5: models, prices and checks
description: Buying a used PS5 in the Netherlands: disc vs digital vs Slim vs Pro, fair prices, how to test the HDMI port, fan and controller, and box-only scams.
intro: A used PS5 is one of the safer electronics buys on Marktplaats, because the console either works or it clearly doesn't, and you can test it in ten minutes. Pay attention to which model you're getting, test the HDMI port and the controller, and never pay for a console you haven't seen running.

sections.heading: Know which PS5 you're looking at
paragraphs: There are four versions on the market. The original 2020 PS5 (model numbers starting with CFI-10, CFI-11 and CFI-12) is the big one with the tall white side panels, sold as a disc edition and a cheaper digital edition. The Slim (CFI-20xx) is smaller and lighter and has a detachable disc drive, so a digital Slim can get a drive added later. The PS5 Pro (CFI-70xx) has no disc drive by default and costs the most.

The model number is on a sticker on the back or bottom and on the box. Ask for a photo of it. A seller who writes 'PS5' without saying disc or digital usually has the digital one, because disc owners mention it.
bullets: Disc edition: plays your physical games and is easier to resell
Digital edition: cheaper, but every game is a download and full price is common
Slim digital: you can buy the external disc drive separately later
Pro: only worth it if you play on a 4K TV and care about frame rates

sections.heading: What to test at the pickup
paragraphs: Ask the seller to have it connected to a TV when you arrive. If that isn't possible, meet somewhere you can plug it in, or bring a portable monitor. A console that 'worked last week' but can't be shown is a gamble.
Let it run a game for at least five minutes. The fan should hum quietly. A loud whine, a rattle or a sudden shutdown points to dust, a failing fan or overheating.
bullets: Look into the HDMI port with your phone torch: bent or missing pins are the most common PS5 repair
Check that the console boots without a 'repair storage' or safe mode screen
Insert a disc (disc models) and make sure it reads and ejects
Plug a controller into each front USB port
Open Settings, System, System Software to see that it updates normally
Compare the serial number on the console with the box

sections.heading: Controllers: stick drift and battery
paragraphs: The DualSense is the weak point. Open a game or the settings menu and let go of both sticks: if the cursor or camera keeps moving on its own, that's stick drift. Press both triggers fully to feel the resistance, test every button, and check that the touchpad clicks.

A worn DualSense lasts noticeably shorter than a new one. If the listing includes two controllers, test both, because a second controller in poor shape is worth almost nothing. A third-party controller in the bundle often isn't worth counting either.

sections.heading: Accounts and digital games
paragraphs: Digital games belong to the seller's PlayStation account, not to the console. A listing that says 'with 20 games' on a digital edition usually means the games disappear when the seller signs out. Only physical discs transfer with the console.

Ask the seller to sign out of their account and do a factory reset in front of you, or check it has already been done. If their account stays on as primary console, you could end up with games you don't own disappearing later.

sections.heading: Scams and listings to skip
paragraphs: Box-only listings ('alleen doos' or 'lege doos') are sometimes worded to look like a console sale at a too-good price. Read the description to the end. Also skip anyone who wants a deposit before you see the console or offers to ship via an unknown courier. Pay on the spot after testing, by bank transfer or cash.
bullets: 'Defect' or 'geen beeld' usually means a damaged HDMI port or APU, not a cheap fix
A Pro for the price of a Slim is almost always a scam
Consoles 'from a bankruptcy sale' with many identical units are a known trick

sections.heading: Finding a good one
paragraphs: Many PS5s come bundled with games, a second controller or a charging dock, and those bundles often price the extras at zero. Compare the console price alone first. On vindje.com you can type something like 'PS5 disc edition with two controllers, under 350 euro, near Utrecht' and skip the box-only listings.

faq.q: Is it safe to buy a used PS5?
faq.a: Yes, if you see it running a game on a TV before paying and the seller removes their account. Most problems (HDMI port, stick drift, fan noise) show up within ten minutes of testing.

faq.q: Can a used PS5 be banned?
faq.a: Sony can restrict accounts and, in rare cases, consoles. It's uncommon, but a console that refuses to connect to the PlayStation Network after a reset is a reason to walk away.

faq.q: Do digital games transfer with a used PS5?
faq.a: No. Digital games stay on the seller's account. Only physical game discs come with the console.

faq.q: Is the PS5 Slim better than the original?
faq.a: It's smaller and quieter in most cases, with the same performance. The original disc edition is often the better deal on the used market.

example_wish: PS5 disc edition with two working controllers, under 330 euro, within 15 km of Amsterdam, no box-only listings

title: Buying a used Nintendo Switch: models, bans and Joy-Con drift
meta_title: Buying a used Nintendo Switch: models and bans
description: Used Nintendo Switch guide: original vs Lite vs OLED vs Switch 2, how to spot a banned or modded console, Joy-Con drift checks and fair prices.
intro: A used Switch is a good buy if you check two things: that the console isn't banned from Nintendo's online services, and that the Joy-Cons don't drift. Pick the model first, because a Lite can't connect to your TV and a Switch 2 costs twice as much.

sections.heading: The four models
paragraphs: The original Switch (2017) and its improved-battery revision (2019) both dock to a TV. The revision lasts noticeably longer on battery; the box says model HAC-001(-01) and is usually red rather than grey. The Switch Lite is handheld only, has fixed controllers and doesn't fit in a dock. The OLED model has a bigger, sharper screen, a better kickstand and a dock with a LAN port. The Switch 2 came out in 2025, plays most Switch 1 games and uses magnetic Joy-Cons.
bullets: Kids and handheld only: Lite
TV and handheld, best value: original revision or OLED
Newest games: Switch 2, which runs Switch 2 exclusives the others can't

sections.heading: Banned and modded consoles
paragraphs: Nintendo bans consoles that have been used with pirated games or custom firmware. A banned Switch still plays cartridges offline, but can't use the eShop, download updates or play online. Sellers don't always know, and some do know and don't say.

At the pickup, connect the console to your phone hotspot and open the Nintendo eShop. If it opens, the console isn't banned. An error code (2124-4007 is the one usually reported for bans) means walk away. Listings mentioning 'gemod', 'CFW', 'unpatched' or a 'chip' are modded. Those are a separate market with ban risk, not a normal family console.
Nintendo has also been reported banning Switch 2 consoles used with copy cartridges, so run the same eShop test on a Switch 2.

sections.heading: Joy-Con drift and other checks
paragraphs: Joy-Con drift is common on the original Joy-Cons and on the Lite's built-in sticks. Go to System Settings, Controllers and Sensors, Calibrate Control Sticks. With the stick untouched, the cross should stay in the middle. Then move each stick in full circles.
bullets: Calibration screen: no drift on either stick
Slide each Joy-Con on and off the console; loose rails make them wobble
Dock the console and check the TV picture (original and OLED)
Look for screen scratches and a bent or yellowed console (heat)
Insert a cartridge and check it loads
Check the charger is the Nintendo one, not a cheap phone charger

sections.heading: Accounts and games
paragraphs: Digital games are tied to the seller's Nintendo Account. If the listing says 'with 15 games' and you see no cartridges in the photos, the games are probably digital and won't stay. Ask the seller to remove their account and do 'Initialize Console' in front of you. Cartridges are the only games that come with the console for sure, and popular ones like Mario Kart 8 Deluxe hold their value, so count them in the price.

sections.heading: Bundles and accessories
paragraphs: Many Switch listings come with a carry case, a Pro Controller, extra Joy-Cons or a pile of cartridges. Price the console first, then add what the extras are worth to you. A genuine Pro Controller is worth EUR 35-50; cheap third-party ones much less. Check that the dock, HDMI cable and the original USB-C charger are all there, since a missing dock on an original or OLED model costs EUR 40-60 to replace.

sections.heading: What's worth paying
paragraphs: Original Switch bundles with a few cartridges are common and often the best deal. The OLED is worth the extra if you play handheld a lot. A Switch 2 makes sense if you want new releases. Replacement Joy-Cons are expensive, so a console with two drifting Joy-Cons should be priced EUR 40-60 lower.
If you want something specific, like an OLED with Mario Kart under 230 euro near you, describing it on vindje.com filters out the bare-box and parts listings.

price_guide.item: Switch original (2019 battery revision), with dock

faq.q: How can I tell if a used Switch is banned?
faq.a: Connect it to the internet and open the eShop. If you get an error instead of the shop, the console is likely banned from online services.

faq.q: Can a banned Switch still play games?
faq.a: Yes, cartridges and already installed games still run offline, but you can't buy games, update or play online. Pay much less, or skip it.

faq.q: Which Switch model is the best buy used?
faq.a: For most people, the 2019 battery revision or the OLED. The Lite suits young kids who only play handheld.

faq.q: Can Joy-Con drift be fixed?
faq.a: Yes, by replacing the stick module, which is cheap but fiddly. Factor it into the price rather than counting on a free repair.

example_wish: Nintendo Switch OLED with Mario Kart 8 cartridge, Joy-Cons without drift, under 240 euro, within 20 km

title: Buying a used camera and lenses: shutter count, fungus and mounts
meta_title: Buying a used camera and lenses: what to check
description: Buying a used camera body or lens: how to check shutter count, spot fungus and haze in lenses, pick the right mount and know fair second-hand prices.
intro: Camera gear is one of the best second-hand categories, because bodies and lenses last for years and lose value fast in the first two. Check the shutter count on bodies, shine a torch through every lens for fungus and haze, and make sure the mount fits what you already own.

sections.heading: Mounts first
paragraphs: A lens only fits bodies with the same mount, so decide on the system before you buy anything. The common ones: Canon EF (DSLR) and RF (mirrorless), Nikon F (DSLR) and Z (mirrorless), Sony E, Fujifilm X and Micro Four Thirds (Olympus/OM System and Panasonic). Canon EF lenses work on RF bodies with Canon's adapter, and Nikon F lenses on Z bodies with the FTZ adapter. Sony E bodies can take many lenses via adapters, but autofocus quality varies.
Older DSLR lenses are cheap now because so many people moved to mirrorless. That makes an EF or F lens plus adapter a good way to save money.

sections.heading: Shutter count on bodies
paragraphs: The shutter is a mechanical part with a rated life. Entry-level DSLRs are often rated around 100,000 actuations, higher-end bodies at 150,000-300,000. A body at 20,000 clicks has lots of life left; one near its rating may need a shutter replacement soon, which can cost more than the body is worth.

For Nikon, Sony, Pentax and Fuji, the count is often in the photo file data and online shutter count readers can show it from an unedited JPEG. For Canon it usually needs a tool that connects to the camera. Ask the seller to send an original JPEG straight from the card. Someone who refuses is a warning sign.

sections.heading: Checking lenses for fungus, haze and dust
paragraphs: Open the aperture (on modern lenses, mount it and hold the depth-of-field button, or look through a lens set to its widest aperture) and shine your phone torch through from the back. Fungus (schimmel) looks like thin threads or spider webs. Haze is a milky fog. A few dust specks are normal and don't show in photos. Fungus and heavy haze are a reason to walk away: cleaning means taking the lens apart, and fungus can etch the glass.
bullets: Torch through the lens: no threads, no fog
Zoom and focus rings turn smoothly, without grinding or dry spots
Aperture blades are dry, not oily
Autofocus finds focus quickly, also in low light
Image stabilization switch works and the image doesn't jump
No dents in the front filter thread, which often means it was dropped

sections.heading: Testing a body at the pickup
paragraphs: Bring your own memory card and take test shots. Shoot a plain wall or sky at f/16 to reveal sensor dust, and at the widest aperture to check focus. Look at the rubber grip (peeling is cosmetic but shows heavy use), the battery door and the card door, and check every button and dial.
Look at the sensor with the lens off (mirrorless) for scratches. Ask why they're selling: upgrading to a new body is a good answer.

sections.heading: Replicas, grey imports and odd listings
paragraphs: Fake cameras are rare, but fake batteries and chargers are common and can swell. Grey-import bodies (meant for another market) work fine but may not get service from the Dutch importer. Very cheap 'like new' bodies with no photos of the actual camera, or sellers who only want to ship, deserve suspicion.

A searchable description helps here: on vindje.com you can ask for something like a Sony A7 III body under 20,000 clicks, no fungus, under 950 euro, and the listings that don't mention it get filtered.

price_guide.item: Canon EOS 80D or Nikon D7200 body

faq.q: What is a good shutter count for a used camera?
faq.a: It depends on the rated life. Under a quarter of the rating is low use, under half is fine, near the rating means you may need a repair soon.

faq.q: Can lens fungus be cleaned?
faq.a: Sometimes, by a repair shop that takes the lens apart. It costs money and can leave etching, so don't pay normal prices for a lens with fungus.

faq.q: Is it better to buy a DSLR or mirrorless used?
faq.a: Mirrorless is where new lenses are going. DSLRs are cheaper and still take great photos, and their lenses can be adapted to mirrorless later.

faq.q: How do I check a camera's shutter count?
faq.a: Ask the seller for an unedited JPEG and use an online shutter count reader, or connect the camera to a manufacturer-specific tool for Canon bodies.

example_wish: Sony A7 III body with low shutter count and original battery, under 950 euro, within 30 km of Rotterdam

title: Buying a used TV: panel types, burn-in and how to test it
meta_title: Buying a used TV: OLED burn-in, panels and testing
description: How to buy a used TV in the Netherlands: OLED vs QLED vs LED, checking burn-in and dead pixels with test images, transport tips and fair prices.
intro: A used TV is good value if you test the screen with plain colour images before you pay. OLEDs can have burn-in, LCD TVs can have clouding and dead backlights, and all of them can have cracked panels that look fine when switched off.

sections.heading: Panel types in plain words
paragraphs: Most TVs are LCD with an LED backlight. 'QLED' (Samsung, TCL, Hisense) and 'NanoCell' are LCD TVs with an extra colour layer. Mini-LED is LCD with many small backlight zones, giving better contrast. OLED (LG, Sony, Philips, Panasonic, Samsung) has pixels that make their own light: perfect blacks, great viewing angles, but some risk of burn-in.
Philips Ambilight TVs are popular in the Netherlands and plenty are on Marktplaats. Ambilight is the coloured light on the wall behind the TV. Test that it works on all sides.

sections.heading: Test images to bring
paragraphs: Put full-screen colour images on a USB stick: white, black, grey (around 20% and 50%), red, green and blue. Or ask the seller to play a 'dead pixel test' video on YouTube. Normal TV content hides most faults.
Look at each image from up close and from your sofa distance.
bullets: Grey screen: look for faint logos, news tickers or game HUDs burned into an OLED
Grey screen: dark corners or patches (clouding) on LCD
Black screen in a dark room: light leaking from the edges (bleed)
Each colour: dead or stuck pixels, vertical or horizontal lines
White screen: pink or green tint in one area, often a failing backlight or panel
Watch the TV for 15 minutes: some faults show only when warm

sections.heading: Burn-in on OLED
paragraphs: Burn-in happens when a static image stays on screen for thousands of hours. OLEDs used as a PC monitor, for 24-hour news or for long gaming sessions are the risk cases. Ask how it was used. Mild burn-in is often only visible on a grey screen and won't bother you in films, but it doesn't go away, so it should be reflected in the price.
Check the hours of use if the TV shows them in a service or settings menu. Low hours on an older set is a good sign.

sections.heading: Smart features, ports and remote
paragraphs: An older smart TV may no longer get app updates, so some streaming apps can stop working. A cheap streaming stick fixes that, so don't overpay for 'smart' on an old set. Check that the remote is included (original remotes can be hard to replace) and that every HDMI port works. For a PS5 or Xbox, look for HDMI 2.1 and 120 Hz support.
Ask the seller to log out of their Netflix and other accounts and to do a factory reset.

sections.heading: Which brands and years hold up
paragraphs: LG's C-series OLEDs (C1, C2, C3) are the most common used OLEDs and a safe pick. Sony and Philips OLEDs use similar panels with different processing. Among LCD sets, Samsung's Q60 and Q70 ranges and Philips mid-range models sell in large numbers, so prices are easy to compare. Very cheap no-name brands often have poor backlights and short software support.
The model number on the back label tells you the year. Look it up before you go so you know the original price and features.

sections.heading: Transport and pickup
paragraphs: Large TVs should be transported upright, ideally in the original box. A flat TV laid on its back in a car with nothing under it can crack. Bring a blanket and a second person for anything 55 inches and up. Check the stand feet and screws are included, and that the panel has no impacts in the corners.
Listings with 'scherm kapot', 'barst' or 'geen beeld' are for parts. Replacing a panel costs about as much as a new TV, so those are only for repairers.

faq.q: How can I check a used OLED for burn-in?
faq.a: Show a full-screen grey image (around 20%) and look for faint shapes such as channel logos or game interfaces. Check from close up and at a slight angle.

faq.q: Is it worth buying a used OLED TV?
faq.a: Yes, if it tests clean on grey and colour screens. OLEDs drop in price fast, so a two or three year old model is often half its new price.

faq.q: Can you lay a TV flat in a car?
faq.a: It's risky, because the panel can bend and crack. Transport it upright and secure it, ideally in its original box.

faq.q: Do old smart TVs still work with Netflix?
faq.a: Some older models lose app support. If that happens, a streaming stick plugged into the HDMI port solves it.

example_wish: LG OLED 55 inch, C1 or newer, no burn-in, with remote and stand, under 550 euro, within 25 km of Utrecht

title: Buying a used computer monitor: panels, ports and pixel checks
meta_title: Buying a used monitor: what to check and pay
description: Used monitor guide: IPS vs VA vs OLED, resolution and refresh rate, USB-C and stands, how to test dead pixels and backlight bleed, and fair prices.
intro: Used monitors are cheap because companies replace them in bulk, and a three year old office screen often works perfectly. Pick the size, resolution and connections you need, then check for dead pixels, backlight bleed and a missing power supply before you pay.

sections.heading: Size and resolution that make sense
paragraphs: At 24 inches, 1080p (1920x1080) looks fine. At 27 inches, 1440p (2560x1440) is the sweet spot for office work and gaming. 4K at 27 inches is very sharp for text and photo work but needs scaling on Windows and a stronger graphics card for games. A 34 inch ultrawide (3440x1440) replaces two screens for many people.
Gamers should look at refresh rate: 144 Hz or 165 Hz feels much smoother than 60 Hz, but only if your PC or console can push those frames.

sections.heading: Panel types
paragraphs: IPS panels have good colours and viewing angles; their typical flaw is 'IPS glow', a lighter haze in corners on dark images that is normal to a degree. VA panels have deeper blacks but can smear in fast motion. TN panels are cheap, fast and look washed out from an angle. OLED monitors are the newest: superb contrast, but burn-in risk if used for static desktop work for long hours.

sections.heading: Connections and stand
paragraphs: Check what your computer has. A monitor with USB-C that delivers power can charge a laptop and carry video over one cable, which is great for a home office. DisplayPort is needed for high refresh rates on many PCs. Older office monitors may have only VGA and DVI, which is a reason to skip them.

Business models from Dell (P and U series), HP (E and Z series) and Lenovo (ThinkVision) usually have stands that go up, down and rotate, plus a VESA mount for a monitor arm. Consumer monitors often tilt only. The stand alone is worth EUR 20-40 to you if your desk is shallow.

sections.heading: How to test at the pickup
paragraphs: Ask the seller to have it connected to a laptop, or bring your own with the right cable. Open full-screen colour images or a dead pixel test page in a browser.
bullets: White, black, red, green, blue screens: no dead or stuck pixels
Black screen in a dim room: no strong light leaking from the edges
Run through all inputs (HDMI, DisplayPort, USB-C)
Check the menu buttons and the brightness setting
Look at the anti-glare coating at an angle for scratches or cleaning marks
Make sure the power cable or external brick is included
Gaming monitor: check the refresh rate in display settings shows 144 Hz or more

sections.heading: Monitors that aren't worth it
paragraphs: Skip 4:3 and 5:4 office screens (1280x1024), monitors with only VGA input, and anything with a yellowed or flickering backlight. Curved budget VA monitors at 1080p and 27 inches look soft because the pixels are large. A cracked or pressure-marked screen can't be repaired at a sensible price.
Monitors with an external power brick are fine, but bricks get lost. Check the exact voltage and connector if the seller has to find it later.

sections.heading: Where the bargains are
paragraphs: Office clearance sellers (search 'bedrijfsontruiming' or 'partij monitoren') sell Dell and HP monitors in batches, usually tested and fairly priced. Sellers who list 'gaming monitor' with RGB lights tend to price high. Check the model number online for the original specs; a 'gaming' monitor may be 75 Hz.
If you want a specific combination, like a 27 inch 1440p screen with USB-C and a height-adjustable stand under 180 euro, describing it on vindje.com saves going through every listing's spec sheet.

price_guide.item: 24 inch 1080p office monitor (Dell P2419H or similar)

faq.q: Is it safe to buy a used monitor?
faq.a: Yes, monitors are simple devices. Test it with colour screens for dead pixels and check every input before paying.

faq.q: How many dead pixels are acceptable?
faq.a: On a used monitor, one dead pixel near the edge is often tolerable if it's reflected in the price. Pixels in the middle of the screen get annoying fast.

faq.q: Is backlight bleed a problem?
faq.a: Mild bleed in a corner on a black screen is common on IPS and rarely visible in normal use. Bright patches visible on dark films are a reason to pass.

faq.q: Can I charge my laptop from a USB-C monitor?
faq.a: Only if the monitor supports USB-C power delivery and gives enough watts for your laptop. Check the model's specs before buying.

example_wish: 27 inch 1440p IPS monitor with USB-C power delivery and height-adjustable stand, under 180 euro, within 15 km of Den Haag

title: Buying used headphones: Sony, Bose, AirPods and how to spot fakes
meta_title: Buying used headphones and AirPods: spot the fakes
description: Buying used Sony, Bose or AirPods headphones: how to spot fake AirPods and Sony XM5s, check battery and noise cancelling, and what a fair price is.
intro: Over-ear noise cancelling headphones are a good second-hand buy: pads can be replaced and the electronics usually last. AirPods are riskier, because fakes are everywhere and look almost identical. Test sound, noise cancelling and battery in person, and pair AirPods with an iPhone before you pay.

sections.heading: The models people sell most
paragraphs: Sony WH-1000XM4 and XM5 are the most common, with the XM6 starting to show up. The XM4 folds up and is still excellent; the XM5 sounds and cancels a bit better but doesn't fold. Bose sells the QuietComfort 45, the QuietComfort Ultra and the older QC35 II, which is comfortable but older tech. Apple: AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4 and AirPods Max.
Earbuds have small batteries that can't be swapped. After three or four years of daily use they may last half as long as new. Over-ear headphones have bigger batteries and age better.

sections.heading: Fake AirPods: how to tell
