paragraphs: Fake AirPods Pro are listed on Marktplaats all the time, often as 'new, unwanted gift' or 'sealed' for EUR 60-90. Many copy a valid serial number from a genuine pair, so checking the serial alone isn't proof. Pair them with an iPhone at the pickup and check the details.
bullets: Settings, Bluetooth, tap the (i): a firmware version and model number should appear
Noise cancelling and transparency mode switch clearly and audibly
Spatial audio and the ear tip fit test work (AirPods Pro)
The case hinge is tight, the magnets snap, the light is centered
Serial on the case matches the serial shown on the iPhone
Sound is full with deep bass, not thin and tinny
A 'sealed' box with poor printing or a loose seal is a red flag

sections.heading: Fake Sony and Bose
paragraphs: Copies of the Sony XM4 and XM5 and of Bose models exist too, usually sold new and too cheap. Install the Sony Headphones Connect app or the Bose app at the pickup: a genuine set connects and shows its model and firmware. Fakes often won't appear in the app at all, have weak noise cancelling and feel light and plasticky.

sections.heading: Checks for any used pair
paragraphs: Wear them for a few minutes. Turn noise cancelling on in a room with background noise (a fridge, traffic) and listen for the drop. Play music and check left and right balance and any crackling at high volume. Ask how long the battery lasts on a full charge.
bullets: Hinges and headband: hairline cracks are common on some models
Ear pads: flaking leatherette is fine if you budget EUR 15-30 for new pads
Touch controls and buttons all respond
Charging port works with a cable you bring
The seller has removed the headphones from their account or app

sections.heading: Battery and ageing
paragraphs: Lithium batteries wear with charge cycles and with age. Over-ear models like the Sony XM4 often still give 20 hours or more after a few years, which is plenty. Earbuds are harder: one bud may die faster than the other. Ask the seller to charge them fully before you arrive, then check the battery level in the app or the iPhone widget after your test. A pair that drops quickly in 10 minutes will disappoint you on a commute.

sections.heading: Single earbuds and hygiene
paragraphs: Listings for 'losse AirPod' (a single left or right bud) or just a case are common, from people who lost one. They can be a cheap way to replace your own missing bud, but must match your model generation. Clean any used earbuds and replace the ear tips; tips cost a few euros.
If you want something like 'Sony XM5 with case, battery still good, under 220 euro near Amsterdam', vindje.com reads the descriptions so you skip the fakes sold 'new in box' with no details.

faq.q: How can I check if AirPods are genuine?
faq.a: Pair them with an iPhone and check that a firmware version shows in Bluetooth settings, then test noise cancelling and spatial audio. A matching serial number alone isn't enough, because fakes copy them.

faq.q: Is it hygienic to buy used earbuds?
faq.a: Yes, if you clean them with alcohol wipes and replace the silicone tips. Over-ear pads can be swapped too.

faq.q: How long does a used AirPods battery last?
faq.a: It depends on age and use. Pairs older than three years often last noticeably shorter than new, so ask and test.

faq.q: Are cheap new AirPods on Marktplaats genuine?
faq.a: Sealed AirPods Pro far below the shop price are very often fake. Treat them with suspicion and test before paying.

example_wish: Sony WH-1000XM5 with original case, good battery, no cracks in the headband, under 220 euro, within 20 km of Amsterdam

title: Buying a used Samsung or Pixel phone: locks, battery and updates
meta_title: Buying a used Samsung or Pixel phone: checks
description: Buying a used Samsung Galaxy or Google Pixel: check Google account lock, IMEI, battery health, screen burn-in and update support before you pay.
intro: A two year old Samsung Galaxy S or Google Pixel costs about half of new and still has years of updates left. The big risk is a phone that is still locked to the seller's Google account or reported stolen. Check the lock, the battery and the screen before money changes hands.

sections.heading: Pick a model with updates left
paragraphs: Security updates matter more than speed. Google promises seven years of updates for the Pixel 8 and later; Samsung does the same for the Galaxy S24 and later. Older models like the Pixel 7 and Galaxy S22 have shorter promises, so check the end-of-support date on the manufacturer's site before buying. A cheap phone with one year of updates left is a short-term buy.

Mid-range Samsungs like the Galaxy A54 and A55 are popular and cheap, with good batteries. Pixels have the best cameras for the money but some older models (Pixel 6 especially) have a mixed reputation for modem and heat issues.

sections.heading: Account lock and stolen phones
paragraphs: Android phones have Factory Reset Protection. If a phone was reset without first removing the Google account, it asks for that account at setup and is unusable without it. Samsung phones can also have a Samsung account lock.

Ask the seller to remove their accounts and do a factory reset in front of you. Then start the setup until you can reach the home screen. Dial *#06# to see the IMEI and compare it with the box and the SIM tray sticker if there is one. A missing box and receipt on a recent flagship is a reason to ask more questions.

sections.heading: Battery health
paragraphs: On Samsung, open the Samsung Members app, go to Diagnostics and run the battery test: it reports the battery as good or not. Newer Pixels (8a and later) show battery health in Settings, Battery. On older Pixels, ask about charging habits and watch the battery percentage during your test. A replacement battery at a repair shop typically costs EUR 60-100.

sections.heading: Screen, camera and the rest
paragraphs: Samsung and Pixel flagships use OLED screens. Open a plain grey or white image and look for burn-in from the keyboard or navigation bar, and for green or pink lines. Some Samsung models have had a green line fault that appears over time.
bullets: Cracks under a screen protector: peel the corner if the seller agrees
Take photos with every camera (wide, ultrawide, zoom, front)
Make a call with your SIM: earpiece and microphone
Test the fingerprint reader and face recognition
Charging port: does it charge with your cable
Speakers at full volume: no buzzing
Check for water damage signs if the seller mentions it 'fell once'

sections.heading: Refurbished grades explained
paragraphs: Shops selling refurbished phones use grades like A, B and C or words like 'als nieuw', 'zeer goed' and 'goed'. These describe the outside: grade C can have clear scratches but should work fully. Private sellers use the same words loosely. Ask for photos of the screen with the phone switched off, at an angle to the light, which shows scratches that normal photos hide.
Storage matters too: 128GB fills up quickly with photos and these phones have no memory card slot.

sections.heading: Prices and what to avoid
paragraphs: Refurbished phones from shops come with warranty and cost a bit more than private sales; that premium is often worth it for a flagship. Avoid 'parts only' phones unless you repair them yourself, and anything sold without a charger and box at a suspiciously low price.
If you know what you want, for example 'Galaxy S23 128GB, battery good, no burn-in, under 300 euro near Eindhoven', vindje.com can filter the listings that don't mention those details.

faq.q: How do I know if a used Android phone is locked?
faq.a: Factory reset it and go through setup. If it asks for a previous Google account, it's still locked and you shouldn't buy it until the seller removes it.

faq.q: How can I check battery health on a Samsung?
faq.a: Use the Samsung Members app, Diagnostics, Battery status. It tells you if the battery is in good condition.

faq.q: Are phones in the Netherlands sim-locked?
faq.a: Most phones sold in the Netherlands are not sim-locked, but some older carrier phones were. Test with your own SIM card at the pickup.

faq.q: Is a used Pixel or Samsung better?
faq.a: Pixels have cleaner software and strong cameras; Samsungs have more choice and better resale value. Both are fine if updates last long enough for you.

example_wish: Samsung Galaxy S23 or Pixel 8, 128GB, battery in good condition, no screen burn-in, under 300 euro, within 20 km

title: Buying vintage hi-fi: amplifiers, receivers and speakers
meta_title: Buying vintage hi-fi: amplifiers and speakers
description: Buying vintage hi-fi on Marktplaats: which Marantz, Pioneer, Technics and Philips amps and speakers to look for, how to test them and what they're worth.
intro: Vintage hi-fi from the 1970s and 1980s can sound excellent and look great, but most of it is 40 years old and needs some work. Test every input and both channels at the pickup, check speaker surrounds for rot, and only pay collector prices for gear that has been serviced.

sections.heading: Names to look for
paragraphs: Silver 1970s receivers from Marantz (2230, 2238, 2252), Pioneer (SX series), Sansui, Kenwood and Yamaha are the classics. They are wanted for the look as much as the sound, so prices have climbed. Technics, Sony and Yamaha amplifiers from the 1980s and early 1990s are often cheaper and sound very good.

The Netherlands has a lot of Philips gear, made in Eindhoven. Philips Motional Feedback (MFB) speakers like the 22RH541 and 22RH545 have built-in amplifiers and have a loyal following. Bang and Olufsen Beomaster receivers are also common here but are sometimes priced on the name.
For speakers, look for KEF, Bowers and Wilkins (DM series), Celestion, Mission, Dynaudio, JBL and Infinity.

sections.heading: Common faults in old amplifiers
paragraphs: Most problems are fixable but cost time or money. Scratchy volume and balance knobs (krakende potmeters) usually clean up with contact cleaner. Dead lamps behind the dial are cosmetic but annoying to replace. A channel that cuts out or hums is more serious, and so is a smell of burning.
A serviced unit ('gereviseerd' or 'nagekeken', often with new capacitors) is worth clearly more. Ask what was done and by whom. 'Recapped' without details means little.

sections.heading: Test checklist for amps and receivers
paragraphs: Bring a phone with a 3.5mm to RCA (tulp) cable and a pair of headphones with a 6.3mm adapter. Ask the seller to have speakers connected.
bullets: Play music on every input (aux, tuner, phono, tape)
Turn the balance fully left and right: both channels work
Turn the volume slowly from zero to loud: listen for crackling
Test speaker A and B switches and the headphone output
Tuner: does it find FM stations and does the needle move
Let it run for 15 minutes: no buzzing, no growing hum, no smell
Look inside through vents for burnt spots or leaking capacitors

sections.heading: Speakers: surrounds and drivers
paragraphs: Many 1970s and 1980s woofers have foam surrounds that crumble with age. Push gently on the edge of the cone: if it's brittle or torn, it needs new surrounds, which is a doable repair (kits cost EUR 20-50) but affects sound if done badly. Rubber surrounds last longer.

Listen to each speaker separately with the balance knob. Check that tweeters work by playing cymbals or a hiss. Pushed-in dust caps can often be pulled out with a vacuum cleaner, but torn cones are a bigger problem. Heavy speakers are best checked before they go in the car.

sections.heading: Transport and setup
paragraphs: Old receivers are heavy and the knobs and dial glass break easily. Wrap the unit in a blanket and keep it flat. Speakers should travel upright with their fronts protected, because a pushed-in tweeter dome is a common transport casualty.

At home, check that the speaker impedance matches the amplifier (most are fine with 8 ohm speakers) and use proper speaker cable. Don't run an old amp at full volume on day one; let it play at normal levels for a while first.

sections.heading: Paying the right price
paragraphs: Prices vary a lot because some sellers list 'vintage' gear at collector prices without servicing it. Compare with completed sales you can find, and remember a full service at a hi-fi repair shop easily costs EUR 100-250. On vindje.com you can describe what you want, like 'serviced Marantz or Pioneer receiver, both channels working, under 400 euro', and skip the 'untested' listings.

price_guide.item: 1980s Technics or Sony stereo amplifier, working
KEF or B&W bookshelf speakers from the 1980s, pair

faq.q: Is vintage hi-fi worth buying?
faq.a: Often yes. A good 1980s amplifier and speakers can sound better than cheap new systems for the same money, as long as they're tested or serviced.

faq.q: What does 'gereviseerd' mean in a listing?
faq.a: It means overhauled: usually cleaned, with worn parts such as capacitors replaced. Ask for details of what was done.

faq.q: How do I fix scratchy volume knobs?
faq.a: Usually with contact cleaner sprayed into the potentiometer while turning it. It often helps, but if it doesn't, the part may need replacing.

faq.q: Can I connect a phone to a vintage amplifier?
faq.a: Yes, with a 3.5mm to RCA cable into an aux or tape input, or with a small Bluetooth receiver.

example_wish: Serviced Marantz or Pioneer receiver from the 1970s, both channels working, no crackling volume, under 450 euro, within 40 km

title: Buying a used record player (platenspeler): models and checks
meta_title: Buying a used record player: models and checks
description: Buying a used record player: belt vs direct drive, Technics, Dual, Pro-Ject and Audio-Technica models, stylus and speed checks, and fair prices.
intro: A good used record player from the 1970s or 1980s often beats a new budget model. The parts that wear are the stylus, the belt and the tonearm bearings, so check those, listen for speed problems and remember you need a phono preamp and speakers too.

sections.heading: Belt drive, direct drive and the ones to skip
paragraphs: Belt drive turntables (Dual, Thorens, Rega, Pro-Ject) use a rubber belt that stretches over time; a new one costs EUR 10-25. Direct drive turntables (Technics, many Japanese decks) have the motor under the platter, start fast and hold speed well. The Technics SL-1200 and SL-1210 are DJ classics and expensive used because they almost never break.

Suitcase players (Crosley and similar) and cheap all-in-one units with built-in speakers have poor tonearms and ceramic cartridges that wear records faster. They're fine as decoration, not for a record collection you care about.

sections.heading: Good models to search for
paragraphs: Dual turntables were very popular in Germany and the Netherlands, so there are many: the 1219, 1229 and the CS 505 series are good value. Thorens TD 160 and TD 166 are solid belt drives. Pro-Ject Debut and Rega Planar 1, 2 and 3 are modern, simple and easy to service. The Audio-Technica AT-LP120 is a common modern direct drive with a built-in preamp, and the AT-LP60X is a basic automatic starter player.
Technics also made cheaper belt and direct drive decks (SL-B and SL-D series) that are a good budget choice.

sections.heading: Stylus and cartridge
paragraphs: The stylus (naald) is the tip that touches the record, held by the cartridge (element). A worn or bent stylus sounds distorted and can damage records. Look at it with your phone camera zoomed in: it should be straight and clean. Ask how old it is. A replacement stylus costs from EUR 20 for basic ones to EUR 100 or more.
A listing that says 'zonder element' has no cartridge at all, which means extra cost of at least EUR 40-80.

sections.heading: Test checklist at the pickup
paragraphs: Bring a record you don't mind playing. Ask the seller to have the player connected to an amplifier with speakers.
bullets: Platter spins at 33 and 45 rpm and reaches speed quickly
Pitch is stable: hold a long piano note and listen for wobble
Use a strobe app on your phone to check speed
Tonearm moves freely, cueing lever lowers it slowly
Automatic models: start and return work
Sound from both channels with no loud hum
Dust cover hinges hold the lid up and the cover isn't cracked

sections.heading: Handling it on the way home
paragraphs: Before transport, lock the tonearm in its rest, remove the counterweight if it unscrews, and take off the platter if possible so the bearing isn't stressed. Tape the dust cover down or carry it separately. On some decks there are transport screws under the platter; ask the seller about them. At home, set the tracking force and anti-skate according to the cartridge specs, which you can look up by its model number.

sections.heading: Phono preamp, amp and speakers
paragraphs: Most turntables need a phono preamp because the cartridge signal is very weak. Vintage amplifiers usually have a phono input; modern ones often don't. Some turntables have a switchable preamp built in ('met ingebouwde voorversterker'). Without one, you'll need a small external preamp (EUR 30-80 used).

If you're starting from scratch, a deck plus a vintage amplifier with a phono input is often cheaper than buying separate modern parts. On vindje.com you can ask for something like 'Dual or Technics turntable with working cartridge, under 200 euro, within 25 km' and leave out listings without a needle.

price_guide.item: Dual 1219 or CS 505, working with cartridge
Pro-Ject Debut Carbon or Rega Planar 2

faq.q: Do I need a preamp for a record player?
faq.a: Yes, unless the turntable has one built in or your amplifier has a phono input. Without it the sound is very quiet and thin.

faq.q: How do I know if a turntable needle is worn?
faq.a: Worn styluses sound harsh or distorted, especially in loud passages and at the end of a side. Zoom in with your phone camera to check it's straight and clean.

faq.q: Is a vintage turntable better than a new cheap one?
faq.a: Often yes. A serviced Dual, Technics or Thorens usually has a better tonearm and motor than a new budget player at the same price.

faq.q: Are suitcase record players bad for records?
faq.a: They use heavy tracking and basic cartridges, which can wear records faster. They're fine for casual listening, not for a valuable collection.

example_wish: Dual or Technics turntable with a working cartridge and new belt, plays 33 and 45, under 200 euro, within 25 km of Haarlem

title: Buying a used Apple Watch: activation lock, battery and fakes
meta_title: Buying a used Apple Watch: activation lock check
description: Buying a used Apple Watch: how to make sure activation lock is off, check battery health, pick GPS or cellular, spot fake Ultras and pay a fair price.
intro: A used Apple Watch is only worth buying if it's removed from the seller's Apple ID, because a locked watch can't be paired and is useless to you. Pair it with your own iPhone at the pickup, check battery health on the watch, and be wary of cheap 'Ultras', which are often fakes.

sections.heading: Activation lock: the one check that matters
paragraphs: When an Apple Watch is paired with an iPhone, Find My turns on activation lock. To remove it, the seller must unpair the watch from their iPhone in the Watch app, which also removes it from their Apple ID. Erasing the watch from the watch itself does not always remove the lock.

Pair the watch with your own iPhone before paying. If it asks for the previous owner's Apple ID password, the lock is still on. Ask the seller to remove it right there; if they can't or won't, don't buy. 'Found' or 'iCloud locked' watches are worth nothing to you.

sections.heading: Battery health
paragraphs: On the watch, open Settings, Battery, Battery Health. Below 80% Apple says the battery has reduced capacity and service is recommended. A watch at 85% or above is fine for a day of normal use. Older watches with worn batteries may not last until bedtime with workouts tracked. Apple's battery service costs around EUR 100, which matters on a watch worth EUR 150.

sections.heading: Which model, size and version
paragraphs: Make sure the watch supports the iPhone you have and still gets watchOS updates. Series 6 and older are close to or past the end of updates; Series 8, Series 9, Series 10, SE (2nd generation) and Ultra models are better choices in 2026. The SE lacks the always-on display and some health sensors but is good value.

Sizes: 40/41/42 mm for smaller wrists, 44/45/46 mm for larger, Ultra 49 mm. GPS + Cellular models can work without your phone nearby, but need a separate watch subscription from your carrier. If you don't need that, a GPS model is cheaper and fine.
bullets: Aluminium case: lighter, scratches more easily
Stainless steel or titanium: sapphire glass, costs more
Check the model and size in Settings, General, About after pairing

sections.heading: Fakes and copies
paragraphs: Copies of the Apple Watch Ultra and Series 9 are sold on Marktplaats, sometimes as 'new, wrong gift'. They look close in photos but don't pair through the Apple Watch app; they use their own apps. If it can't pair with an iPhone via the Watch app, it isn't an Apple Watch. Also check the weight and the quality of the Digital Crown, which on copies feels loose.

sections.heading: Cellular models and the eSIM
paragraphs: A cellular watch from a carrier deal works with any Dutch carrier that supports Apple Watch, but the seller should remove their watch plan first. If they forget, you may see a message about the previous plan during setup; usually it can be removed from the watch. Ask the seller to cancel or transfer their watch subscription so you don't end up with a number tied to their account.
Health data and Apple Pay cards are erased when the watch is unpaired, so there's no privacy risk for either of you once that's done.

sections.heading: Physical checks
paragraphs: Look closely at the screen for scratches and cracks, especially on aluminium models with Ion-X glass. Press the side button and turn the crown. Check the back sensor glass for cracks. Make sure the charger is included; third-party chargers often don't work with newer watches. Straps are easy to replace, so don't pay extra for them.
If you want a specific spec, like an Apple Watch Series 9 45mm GPS with battery over 90% under 250 euro, vindje.com can read the listings for battery and size details.

faq.q: How do I check if a used Apple Watch is locked?
faq.a: Try to pair it with your own iPhone. If it asks for the previous owner's Apple ID, activation lock is still on and the seller must remove it.

faq.q: What battery health is OK on a used Apple Watch?
faq.a: Above 85% is good for a full day. Below 80% means reduced capacity and probably a battery service soon.

faq.q: Can I use a cellular Apple Watch without a subscription?
faq.a: Yes, it works as a normal GPS watch when you don't add a cellular plan.

faq.q: Will an old Apple Watch work with my iPhone?
faq.a: Only if both run compatible software. Check that the watch model still gets watchOS updates for your iPhone's iOS version.

example_wish: Apple Watch Series 9 45mm GPS, battery health above 90%, removed from Apple ID, with charger, under 250 euro, within 20 km

title: Buying a used washing machine: brands, age and how to test it
meta_title: Buying a used washing machine: brands and checks
description: Buying a used washing machine (wasmachine): which brands last, how to find its age, bearing and seal checks, transport bolts and fair prices.
intro: A used washing machine is a sensible buy if it's from a brand that lasts, is less than about eight years old, and passes a quick check of the drum bearings and door seal. Bring the transport bolts back into the picture before you move it, because a drum bouncing loose in a van can wreck the machine.

sections.heading: Brands that last
paragraphs: Miele is the brand people pay extra for second hand, because their machines are built for a long life and parts stay available for years. A ten year old Miele in good shape can still be a better buy than a three year old budget machine. Bosch and Siemens (made by the same company) are the solid middle ground and very common on Marktplaats. AEG, Samsung and LG are fine too, though some cheaper models from any brand have sealed drums that make a bearing repair uneconomic.
Very cheap no-name machines are usually not worth the transport effort.

sections.heading: Finding out how old it is
paragraphs: Sellers often guess the age. The type plate, inside the door rim or on the back, has the model and serial number. For Bosch and Siemens, the FD number on the plate encodes the production month and year, and FD decoders online turn it into a date. For Miele and others, searching the model number tells you roughly which years it was sold. An old machine isn't automatically bad, but price it accordingly.

sections.heading: Checks at the pickup
paragraphs: Ask the seller not to disconnect the machine before you arrive, so you can see it run a short program. If it's already disconnected, you can still do most checks by hand.
bullets: Bearings: lift the drum up and down from the inside; more than a little play or a clunk is bad
Spin the drum by hand: smooth and quiet, no rumbling or grinding
Door seal (manchet): no tears, holes or black mould deep in the folds
Detergent drawer: no thick limescale or mould, comes out freely
Door lock clicks and the handle isn't broken
Look under the machine for rust or water marks
Ask about error codes or programs that stop halfway
Run a quick rinse and spin if it's still connected: listen for loud banging

sections.heading: Size, capacity and energy
paragraphs: Standard machines are 60 cm wide and about 85 cm high, fitting under a counter. Depth varies from about 45 to 65 cm, which matters in a small Dutch bathroom or attic. Measure your spot including the tap and drain. Capacity of 7-8 kg suits most households; 9 kg and up is for families.

Energy and water use improved a lot in the last 15 years, but a washing machine uses far less electricity than a dryer, so a slightly older model with good build quality is often fine. Washer-dryer combinations (was-droogcombinatie) save space but are slower and fail more often than two separate machines.

sections.heading: Transport bolts and moving it
paragraphs: Front loaders have transport bolts (transportbeveiliging or transportschroeven) at the back that lock the drum. Ask if the seller still has them. Without them, the drum swings on its shocks during transport and can damage the springs or tub. Universal replacement bolts exist, or you can wedge the drum carefully, but the original bolts are best.

Drain the leftover water via the small filter hatch at the front bottom before you load it, or it will leak in your car. A washing machine weighs 65-85 kg, so bring a hand truck and a second person, and remove the bolts again before the first wash.

sections.heading: When to skip
paragraphs: Skip machines that smell of burnt motor, leak, have a cracked drum spider ('lekt' or 'maakt lawaai bij centrifugeren' in the listing), or are free because they 'need a small repair'. Small repairs on washing machines are often bearings, and that is not small. On vindje.com you can describe what you need, like a Bosch or Miele wasmachine under seven years old, 8 kg, under 250 euro and within 15 km, and skip the defect ones.

faq.q: How long does a washing machine last?
faq.a: Many budget machines last around 8-10 years; Miele designs for a longer life. Use and maintenance matter more than the age on paper.

faq.q: How do I check the bearings on a used washing machine?
faq.a: Lift the drum up and down and spin it by hand. Noticeable play, clunking or a grinding sound means worn bearings.

faq.q: Can I move a washing machine without transport bolts?
faq.a: It's risky, because the drum can swing and damage the suspension. Use the original bolts if possible or buy universal ones.

faq.q: Is a used Miele worth the extra money?
faq.a: Often yes. Miele machines are built to last longer and parts are easier to get, so a used Miele in good shape usually outlives a cheaper newer machine.

example_wish: Bosch or Miele washing machine, 8 kg, less than 7 years old, with transport bolts, under 250 euro, within 15 km of Utrecht

title: Buying a used dryer: heat pump vs condenser vs vented
meta_title: Buying a used dryer: heat pump vs condenser
description: Buying a used dryer in the Netherlands: heat pump vs condenser vs vented, what the energy difference costs, which checks to do and fair second-hand prices.
intro: For most people in the Netherlands, a used heat pump dryer (warmtepompdroger) is the best buy: it uses roughly half the electricity of a condenser dryer, which pays back quickly at Dutch energy prices. Check that the heat pump does its job, that all filters are present and clean, and let it stand upright for a few hours after transport.

sections.heading: Three types, quick comparison
paragraphs: A vented dryer (afvoerdroger or luchtafvoerdroger) blows warm, wet air outside through a hose, so it needs a window or wall opening. It's simple, cheap and fast, but uses a lot of energy. A condenser dryer (condensdroger) collects the water in a tank or drains it and needs no hose, but also heats with a big element. A heat pump dryer recycles the heat, works at lower temperatures (kinder to clothes) and uses much less power, at the cost of longer drying times.

As a rough idea, a condenser dryer uses several kilowatt hours per full load and a heat pump dryer about half or less. If you dry a few loads a week, the difference adds up to a lot of money per year, which is why heat pump dryers hold their value.
bullets: Small flat without outside wall: heat pump or condenser
Rarely dry clothes and tight budget: condenser
Attic with a window and very occasional use: vented is fine

sections.heading: What to check on a heat pump dryer
paragraphs: Heat pump dryers have a sealed refrigerant circuit, like a fridge. If that circuit fails, the repair is usually not worth it. Ask the seller to run a program for 10-15 minutes before you arrive. The air inside the drum should be warm and the machine should hum steadily. If the drum is still cold after 15 minutes, the compressor may be dead.
bullets: Door filter (pluizenfilter) present and not torn
Second filter at the bottom (plinth or heat exchanger filter) present and not caked with lint
Heat exchanger fins behind it not blocked or bent
Water tank present, slides out, not cracked
Drum turns both ways and stops without scraping
No error code or 'clean heat exchanger' message that won't clear

sections.heading: Brands and what to pay
paragraphs: Miele heat pump dryers (T1 range) have a reputation for lasting and many have a self-cleaning heat exchanger, so they need less filter care. Bosch, Siemens and AEG are common and reliable. Some cheaper brands have more problems with the heat pump circuit. Look up the model number to see its age and energy label.
A dryer that has been neglected (filters full of lint for years) runs longer and hotter, which wears it out. The condition of the filters tells you a lot about the owner.

sections.heading: Transport and first use
paragraphs: Heat pump dryers and condenser dryers with a heat pump should be moved upright if you can. If it had to lie down, the common advice is to let it stand upright for several hours before switching it on, so the compressor oil settles. Empty the water tank before moving it. Dryers can stack on a washing machine with a stacking kit (tussenstuk) made for that combination, never by just placing them on top.

sections.heading: Listings to avoid
paragraphs: Avoid 'droogt niet meer goed' (doesn't dry well anymore), which on a heat pump model often means a refrigerant leak. 'Free, works but slow' on a heat pump dryer is also a warning sign. Condenser dryers that take two cycles to dry a load often have a blocked condenser, which you can clean, but check it's there and intact.
On vindje.com you can ask for a heat pump dryer under eight years old, with both filters, under 250 euro within 20 km, and the condenser and vented models get filtered out.

price_guide.item: Bosch, Siemens or AEG heat pump dryer, 3-7 years old

faq.q: Is a heat pump dryer worth it second hand?
faq.a: Usually yes, because the energy saving over a condenser dryer is large at Dutch electricity prices. Just make sure the heat pump still produces heat.

faq.q: Why does a heat pump dryer take so long?
faq.a: It dries at a lower temperature, so a cycle takes longer. Clogged filters make it much slower, so clean both of them.

faq.q: Can you lay a heat pump dryer down for transport?
faq.a: It's better to keep it upright. If it has been on its side, let it stand upright for several hours before switching it on.

faq.q: Can I put a dryer on top of my washing machine?
faq.a: Only with a stacking kit that fits both models. Without it, the dryer can vibrate off.

example_wish: Heat pump dryer (warmtepompdroger) from Miele, Bosch or Siemens, under 8 years old, both filters included, under 300 euro, within 20 km

title: Buying a used fridge or freezer: types, sizes and checks
meta_title: Buying a used fridge or freezer: what to check
description: Buying a used fridge or freezer (koelkast, vriezer): freestanding vs built-in sizes, energy use, door seals, cooling checks and transport tips.
intro: A used fridge is a good deal if it cools properly, the door seals close tight and it fits your space. Built-in fridges must match your kitchen niche to the centimetre, and very old fridges can cost more in electricity than you save on the price.

sections.heading: Freestanding or built-in
paragraphs: Freestanding fridges (vrijstaand) just need a socket and some room for air at the back. Built-in fridges (inbouw) go into a kitchen cabinet with the cabinet door fixed to the fridge door. Their niche heights are standard: about 88 cm (under the counter), 102, 122, 140, 158 and 178 cm. Measure your niche height and check how the door is fixed: sliding door (sleepdeur) or fixed hinge door (deur-op-deur). The new fridge must match the system, or you'll need different mounting hardware.
American fridges (Amerikaanse koelkast) are about 90 cm wide and very deep. Check your door frames and the stairs before you buy one, since many Dutch houses have narrow stairwells.

sections.heading: Age and energy use
paragraphs: A fridge runs day and night, so energy use matters more than for most appliances. Fridges from the last 10 years are much more efficient than those from the early 2000s. The energy label scale changed in 2021, so an old 'A+' and a new 'E' can mean similar use; compare the kWh per year printed on the label instead. A big old American fridge or a chest freezer from the 1990s can use several hundred kWh per year.
Look up the model number on the type plate inside the fridge to find its age.

sections.heading: Checks at the pickup
paragraphs: Ask the seller to keep the fridge running until you arrive. Bring a simple thermometer or put your hand inside: the fridge should be cold, around 4 degrees, and the freezer frozen solid.
bullets: Door seals: close the door on a sheet of paper; it should be hard to pull out all around
No cracks in the inner plastic, especially around shelves and door bins
All shelves, drawers and egg trays present (replacements are pricey)
No smell that stays after cleaning
Freezer: no thick ice buildup, which can mean a bad seal or defrost fault
No-frost freezer: ice on the back wall points to a defrost problem
Compressor runs with a low hum, no loud clicking every few minutes
Water or ice dispenser (American fridges): test it and ask about the filter

sections.heading: Transport and switching on
paragraphs: Move fridges upright when you can. If it had to lie down, let it stand upright before switching it on so the compressor oil can flow back. A common rule is to wait at least as long as it was lying down, and a few hours at minimum. Tape the doors shut and take out glass shelves. Defrost and dry a freezer before moving it, or water ends up in your car.

sections.heading: Cleaning before use
paragraphs: Clean the inside with warm water and a bit of soda or vinegar, including the door seals and the small drain hole at the back wall of the fridge, which can block and cause water under the vegetable drawers. Leave the doors open for a while to air out. Let it run empty for a few hours to reach temperature before you put food in.

sections.heading: Freezers and small fridges
paragraphs: Chest freezers (vrieskist or diepvrieskist) are cheap second hand and simple, but check the lid seal and the lid hinge, which tends to sag. Upright freezers with drawers are easier to use. Tabletop fridges (tafelmodel) are popular for student rooms. For a Smeg retro fridge, prices stay high because of the look; check for rust under the seal and on the door hinges.

If you need a specific size, like a built-in fridge for a 122 cm niche with a sleepdeur, vindje.com lets you describe exactly that with a price and distance, instead of reading every listing for measurements.

faq.q: How long should a fridge stand before switching on after transport?
faq.a: If it was transported upright, a short wait is enough. If it lay down, wait at least as long as it was lying, and a few hours minimum.

faq.q: Is it worth buying an old fridge?
faq.a: Only if it's in good shape and not too old. A fridge from before around 2010 can use a lot more electricity, eating up the savings.

faq.q: What sizes do built-in fridges come in?
faq.a: Standard niche heights are about 88, 102, 122, 140, 158 and 178 cm. Measure yours and check the door mounting system.

faq.q: How can I test if a used fridge cools?
faq.a: Ask the seller to keep it running, then check that the fridge is cold and the freezer is frozen. A thermometer gives you a clear answer.

example_wish: Built-in fridge for a 122 cm niche with sleepdeur system, less than 8 years old, working, under 200 euro, within 15 km of Amersfoort

title: Buying a used dishwasher: sizes, brands and what to check
meta_title: Buying a used dishwasher: sizes and checks
description: Buying a used dishwasher (vaatwasser) in the Netherlands: freestanding vs integrated, 45 or 60 cm, brands that last, leak and rust checks and fair prices.
intro: A used dishwasher is cheap and usually reliable, but only if it fits your kitchen and has no hidden leak. Measure the width and niche height first, then check the spray arms, filter, racks and the bottom tray, where a leak shows up first.

sections.heading: Which type fits your kitchen
paragraphs: Freestanding dishwashers (vrijstaand) have their own top and front and stand anywhere near a tap and drain. Built-in ones come in two kinds: fully integrated (volledig geïntegreerd), where your kitchen door covers the whole front and the controls are on the top edge, and semi-integrated (half geïntegreerd), with a visible control panel. An undercounter freestanding model can also go under a counter if you remove its top.

Standard width is 60 cm; narrow models are 45 cm. Niche height for built-in is usually 82-87 cm, with some 'XXL' models needing about 86-92 cm. Measure your space and check the door hinge type if your cabinet door is heavy.

sections.heading: Brands and age
paragraphs: Bosch and Siemens (made by the same company) dominate the Dutch market, so there are plenty of used ones and spare parts are easy to find. Miele lasts longer and has excellent racks; it costs more used. AEG, Beko and others are fine. The model and serial number are on a sticker on the side of the door. For Bosch and Siemens, the FD number on that sticker encodes the production date.
Dishwashers often run 10 years or more. One that's five years old and well kept has plenty of life left.

sections.heading: Checks at the pickup
paragraphs: Open the door and pull out both racks. Most problems are visible.
bullets: Spray arms turn freely and their holes aren't blocked
Filter at the bottom: present, not broken, not full of grease
Racks: wheels intact, no rust on the tines (rust stains glasses)
Door springs: the door stays where you leave it, doesn't slam open
Inner tub: no rust spots or cracks
Door seal: soft and intact
Detergent and rinse aid compartments open and close
Tilt it slightly: water sloshing in the base points to a leak
Ask about error codes, such as a leak or water supply code

sections.heading: Leaks and the AquaStop hose
paragraphs: Many dishwashers have a leak sensor in the base. When water collects there, the machine stops and pumps continuously, showing an error. On Bosch and Siemens, E15 is the well-known code for this. Sometimes it's a loose hose, sometimes a cracked part. Ask whether it ever happened.
The inlet hose with the thick box near the tap is an AquaStop: it shuts the water off if the hose bursts. Check it isn't cut or kinked, because the whole hose has to be replaced if it's damaged.

sections.heading: Cleaning a used dishwasher before first use
paragraphs: Even a good used dishwasher has old grease in it. Take out the filter and wash it with hot water and a brush, clear any food from the spray arm holes with a toothpick, and wipe the door seal and the bottom edge of the door, where dirt collects. Then run an empty hot program with a dishwasher cleaner or a cup of vinegar on the top rack. Fill the salt container if your water is hard, because a machine that ran without salt for months may leave white film on glasses at first.

sections.heading: Moving and installing
paragraphs: Drain the dishwasher before moving it by running a quick drain cycle or tipping it slightly over a towel. Tape the door shut and take out the cutlery basket. Installing a fully integrated dishwasher means mounting your kitchen door on it, which takes some patience. If your previous one was a different brand, the door may need new holes.
If you need a specific fit, like a fully integrated 60 cm Bosch dishwasher for a 82 cm niche under 200 euro, you can describe that on vindje.com and leave out the freestanding ones.

price_guide.item: Bosch or Siemens freestanding, 3-6 years old

faq.q: How long does a dishwasher last?
faq.a: Ten years or more is common for well-kept machines. Check the production year on the door sticker.

faq.q: What does error E15 mean on a Bosch dishwasher?
faq.a: It means water was detected in the base tray, often from a leak. It can be minor or serious, so be careful with a used machine showing it.

faq.q: Can a freestanding dishwasher go under the counter?
faq.a: Many can, after removing the top panel, but check the model's height without the top and your niche height.

faq.q: What is the difference between integrated and semi-integrated?
faq.a: Fully integrated models are hidden behind a kitchen door with controls on top; semi-integrated show a control panel above the door.

example_wish: Fully integrated Bosch or Siemens dishwasher, 60 cm, fits 82 cm niche, under 6 years old, under 200 euro, within 15 km

title: Buying a used espresso machine: bean-to-cup and portafilter
meta_title: Buying a used espresso machine: what to check
description: Buying a used espresso machine: bean-to-cup (volautomaat) vs portafilter, Jura, DeLonghi, Philips and Gaggia, brew group checks and fair prices.
intro: A used espresso machine can save you hundreds of euros, but limescale and worn seals hide inside. With bean-to-cup machines (volautomaat), check the brew group, the cup counter and the descaling history. With portafilter machines, check the pressure, the temperature and the group head seal.

sections.heading: Bean-to-cup or portafilter
paragraphs: A bean-to-cup machine grinds, tamps and brews at the press of a button. DeLonghi Magnifica, Philips series 2200 to 5400, Siemens EQ and Jura are the common ones. They're easy and make decent coffee and milk drinks. A portafilter machine (pistonmachine in everyday Dutch) needs a separate grinder and some skill, but makes better espresso and lasts longer, because it's a simpler machine. Gaggia Classic, Rancilio Silvia, Lelit, ECM, Rocket and the Sage (Breville) Barista range are common.
If you just want good coffee every morning without fuss, a well-kept bean-to-cup is the right choice. If you enjoy the process, go portafilter.

sections.heading: Checks for bean-to-cup machines
paragraphs: Ask the seller to make a coffee and a milk drink while you watch.
bullets: Brew group: on DeLonghi, Philips and Siemens it comes out from the side; check it's clean, greased and not cracked
Jura machines have a non-removable brew group; ask when it was last serviced
Cup counter: many machines show the number of drinks in a menu; above 15,000-20,000 means heavy use
Grinder makes an even sound and produces coffee grounds, not a whine
Coffee comes out hot and with crema, not watery
Milk system froths, and the milk tubes are clean
Drip tray and grounds container: look for water underneath, a sign of a leak
Ask how often it was descaled and with what

sections.heading: Checks for portafilter machines
paragraphs: Bring some ground coffee if the seller has no grinder. Let the machine heat up fully, which takes 10-30 minutes depending on the model. A machine with a pressure gauge should reach around 9 bar during a shot. Steam should be dry and strong.
bullets: Group head gasket: dry or cracked rubber leaks during a shot
Shower screen: not clogged with old coffee
Steam and hot water valves close fully, no dripping
No limescale crust inside the water tank or around the valves
Boiler doesn't hiss or leak underneath
Accessories: portafilter, baskets, tamper (a proper tamper adds EUR 20-40)

sections.heading: Limescale: the hidden problem
paragraphs: Hard tap water in parts of the Netherlands builds scale fast. A machine that was never descaled can have clogged pipes and a weak heating element. Ask if a water filter was used, and look at the inside of the water tank and the hot water outlet. White crust is a bad sign. A dual-boiler machine with heavy scale can cost hundreds to clean.
Never buy a 'only needs descaling' machine that doesn't run at all, because descaling rarely fixes a fully blocked machine.

sections.heading: Grinder and running costs
paragraphs: With a portafilter machine, the grinder matters as much as the machine. A basic blade grinder won't work; you need a burr grinder that grinds fine and evenly, which adds EUR 80-300 used. Bean-to-cup machines have the grinder built in, but you'll spend on descaler, cleaning tablets and sometimes water filters. Also budget for a new set of gaskets on an older portafilter machine. They cost little and fix most leaks around the group head.

sections.heading: Where the deals are
paragraphs: Bean-to-cup machines lose value fast, so a three year old DeLonghi or Philips is often a third of its new price. Good portafilter machines like a Rancilio Silvia or Lelit hold their price. Office clearances sometimes sell Jura machines with very high counters; those need a service. On vindje.com you can ask for something like 'Philips or DeLonghi bean-to-cup with milk frother, under 20,000 cups, under 200 euro' and skip the listings that don't say.

faq.q: How do I check how many cups a used coffee machine has made?
faq.a: Most bean-to-cup machines have a statistics or counter menu in the settings. Look up the model's manual to find it.

faq.q: Is a used Jura worth it?
faq.a: A Jura with a recent service and a moderate cup count can be a good buy. One with a very high counter and no service history probably needs an expensive overhaul soon.

faq.q: How often should an espresso machine be descaled?
faq.a: It depends on your water hardness and use, usually every few weeks to months. The machine often tells you, or follow the manual.

faq.q: Should I buy a bean-to-cup or a portafilter machine?
faq.a: Bean-to-cup is easier and faster; portafilter makes better espresso, needs a good grinder and lasts longer.

example_wish: Philips or DeLonghi bean-to-cup coffee machine with milk frother, less than 20,000 cups, regularly descaled, under 200 euro, within 20 km

title: Buying a used Dyson vacuum: batteries, models and fakes
meta_title: Buying a used Dyson vacuum: battery and fake checks
description: Buying a used Dyson V8, V10, V11 or V15: how to test the battery, spot fake chargers and batteries, check the motor and filter, and what to pay.
intro: A used Dyson stick vacuum is good value if the battery still holds a charge, because a worn battery is the main reason people sell them. Run it on the highest setting at the pickup, watch how long it lasts, and check that the charger and battery are genuine Dyson parts.

sections.heading: Which model is which
paragraphs: The V8 (2016) is the oldest you'll still see often. It has a trigger and gives up to about 40 minutes when new on the lowest setting. The V10 has a bigger bin and more power. The V11 adds an LCD screen that shows remaining runtime, which makes a battery check easy. The V12 Detect Slim is lighter with a laser head. The V15 Detect has a laser head and a dust sensor, and the Gen5 Detect is the newer top model.
Model names are printed on the body, and the serial number sticker is behind the bin or on the battery side. Search the model before the pickup so you know which attachments should come with it.

sections.heading: Battery: the thing to test
paragraphs: Dyson batteries wear with use, and a worn one runs only a few minutes, especially on max power. Ask the seller to charge it fully before you arrive. Then run it on boost or max for a minute: it should keep running smoothly. On the V11, V15 and Gen5 the screen shows the remaining minutes, so you can see the estimate right away.

Pulsing (the motor switching on and off rapidly) usually means a blocked filter or airflow, or a failing battery. Clean the filter first if the seller agrees and try again. A flashing red light on the battery often means a battery fault.

Replacing the battery is possible on most models. On the V8 and V10 the battery is held by two screws; some newer models have a click-in battery. Official Dyson batteries cost much more than aftermarket ones, and cheap aftermarket batteries vary in quality.

sections.heading: Fakes and copies
paragraphs: Complete fake Dyson stick vacuums are less common than fake hair tools, but fake parts are everywhere: batteries, chargers, filters and attachments. Fake chargers are a fire risk. Look for the Dyson logo moulded into the charger, a proper weight, and a label with clear printing. Batteries should have the Dyson logo and a matching part number.
Listings for a 'Dyson-style' or 'compatible' vacuum are not Dysons, even if the photo looks like one. If a V15 is priced like a V8, ask for a photo of the serial sticker.

sections.heading: Checklist at the pickup
paragraphs: Go through this list with the seller before any money changes hands.
bullets: Runs on all power modes without pulsing
Battery lasts at least several minutes on max
Bin opens and empties, the latch isn't cracked
Cyclone and filter not broken, filter not caked with dust
Main floor head brush spins, laser head lights up (Detect models)
Charger is Dyson and charges the battery (light shows)
No burning smell from the motor
Wall dock and attachments included as listed

sections.heading: Corded Dysons and older models
paragraphs: Corded upright and cylinder Dysons (the Ball and Big Ball range, the DC series) are cheap second hand and have no battery to wear out. They're heavy but suction stays consistent. For a large house with lots of carpet, a corded model for EUR 50-100 can be a better buy than a stick vacuum with a tired battery. Check the hose for splits and the brush bar for wrapped hair, and listen for a loud whining motor.

sections.heading: Parts-only listings and repairs
paragraphs: Listings saying 'accu defect' or 'voor onderdelen' are sold for parts. With a new battery at EUR 40-120 they can make sense for a V10 or V11 in otherwise good shape, but you're gambling that the motor and trigger work. The motor itself isn't economical to replace.
If you want something specific, like a Dyson V11 with a battery that still lasts 20 minutes under 200 euro near you, vindje.com filters out the parts-only and 'compatible' listings for you.

faq.q: How long does a Dyson battery last?
faq.a: Several years with normal use, but runtime drops gradually. A battery that dies in under five minutes on the medium setting is worn.

faq.q: Why does my Dyson pulse on and off?
faq.a: Usually a blocked filter or airflow, or a failing battery. Clean the filter and check for blockages first.

faq.q: Can you replace a Dyson battery?
faq.a: Yes. Most V-series batteries are replaceable with a screwdriver or a click, either official or aftermarket.

faq.q: How do I know if a Dyson charger is fake?
faq.a: Fake chargers often feel light, have poor printing and no proper Dyson logo. Use only genuine or well-known brand chargers, because cheap ones can overheat.

example_wish: Dyson V11 or V15 stick vacuum, battery still runs 20 minutes, original charger, under 230 euro, within 20 km of Rotterdam

title: Buying a used oven or combi-microwave: sizes, power and checks
meta_title: Buying a used oven or combi microwave: checks
description: Buying a used built-in oven or combi microwave (combimagnetron): niche sizes, power and plugs, how to test heating elements and fair prices.
intro: A used built-in oven or combi microwave (combimagnetron) is one of the easier appliances to buy second hand: few moving parts and easy to test. Get the niche size right, check what plug and power it needs, and test every heating mode before you pay.

sections.heading: Types and sizes
paragraphs: A standard built-in oven (inbouwoven) fits a 60 cm high niche. A compact oven or combi microwave fits a 45 cm high niche; both are 60 cm wide. A combimagnetron combines a microwave with a hot-air oven and grill, popular in Dutch kitchens without space for two appliances. Steam ovens (stoomoven) and combi-steam ovens are also compact, 45 cm.

Measure the niche height, width and depth, plus the space for air at the back. Built-in ovens are fixed by screws through the front frame into the cabinet, so the frame size of the new unit should cover your opening.
Freestanding ovens and countertop combi microwaves need no niche at all, which is the easy option in a rental.

sections.heading: Power and plugs
paragraphs: Most built-in ovens and combi microwaves have a normal plug and draw up to around 3.5 kW. Ideally they get their own group in the fuse box, especially if your induction hob is on the same circuit. A freestanding range (fornuis) with an induction or ceramic hob usually needs a perilex socket or a dedicated connection. Check the type plate and the plug before buying, and ask an electrician if you're unsure; don't improvise with extension cables.

sections.heading: How to test at the pickup
paragraphs: Ask the seller to keep the oven connected. If it's been removed from the kitchen, ask them to plug it in somewhere so you can test it, or see a video of it running with the display on.
bullets: Top heat, bottom heat, hot air and grill each warm up within a few minutes
Fan runs quietly without grinding
Oven light works, the clock and timer can be set
Microwave function: heat a cup of water for one minute, it should be hot
Door closes firmly, the inner glass isn't cracked, the seal is intact
Interior enamel without chips or rust
Pyrolysis models: check the door locks when you start a cleaning program
Racks and baking trays included (replacements cost EUR 15-40 each)

sections.heading: Brands and features worth paying for
paragraphs: Bosch, Siemens, Neff, AEG, Miele and Atag are common in Dutch kitchens. Atag and Pelgrim are Dutch brands found in many new-build homes; spare parts are available. Pyrolytic self-cleaning saves a lot of scrubbing. Telescopic rails make heavy trays safer. A built-in meat probe is nice but most cooks manage without one.

Combi microwaves from Miele and Bosch hold their value. Very cheap combi microwaves with a weak grill often disappoint as ovens, so check the hot air function uses a proper convection fan, not just a grill element.

sections.heading: Cleaning and first use
paragraphs: A used oven that looks dirty inside isn't a problem in itself; a pyrolytic model can clean itself in a few hours, and a normal enamel interior cleans up with soda and patience. What matters is the heating and the door. Before cooking, run the empty oven at 200 degrees for half an hour with a window open to burn off any residue. For a combi microwave, clean the cavity well first, because food splashes can scorch when heated by the grill.

sections.heading: Things to skip
paragraphs: Avoid ovens with a microwave that sparks or runs without heating, a cracked inner door glass, or rust inside the microwave cavity, because microwaves with internal damage can be unsafe. Also avoid units removed from a kitchen with the wires cut short and no plug, unless you'll have it connected professionally.
On vindje.com you can search for something like 'built-in combi microwave, 45 cm niche, Bosch or Siemens, under 200 euro within 15 km' and skip the countertop models.

price_guide.item: Built-in oven, Bosch or Siemens, 3-8 years old

faq.q: What size niche does a combimagnetron need?
faq.a: Built-in combi microwaves usually need a niche about 45 cm high and 56-60 cm wide. Check the installation size in the model's manual.

faq.q: Does a built-in oven need its own group?
faq.a: It's recommended, especially combined with an induction hob. Check the fuse box and ask an electrician if unsure.

faq.q: How can I test a used microwave?
faq.a: Heat a cup of water for a minute. It should be clearly hot, and there should be no sparking or burning smell.

faq.q: Is it safe to buy a used microwave?
faq.a: Yes, if the door closes properly and the cavity and seal are undamaged. Skip any with rust holes or a damaged door.

example_wish: Built-in combi microwave for a 45 cm niche, Bosch, Siemens or Miele, all functions working, under 200 euro, within 15 km

title: Buying a used mobile air conditioner (mobiele airco)
meta_title: Buying a used mobile air conditioner: what to check
description: Buying a used mobile air conditioner (mobiele airco): single vs dual hose, BTU sizing, why air coolers aren't airco, what to test and when prices drop.
intro: A used mobile airco is a smart buy in autumn or winter, when sellers want the space back and prices drop. Make sure it's a compressor airco with an exhaust hose, not an air cooler, and test that it blows cold within a few minutes before you pay.

sections.heading: Airco or air cooler
paragraphs: A mobile air conditioner has a compressor and a wide hose that blows hot air out of a window. An air cooler (luchtkoeler or aircooler) is a fan that blows over water or ice. Air coolers add humidity and lower the temperature only slightly, and in a humid Dutch summer they often make a room feel worse. Many listings mix up the words.
Rule of thumb: no thick exhaust hose means no airco. A device under about 10 kg with a water tank you fill is a cooler.

sections.heading: Size and type
paragraphs: Capacity is listed in BTU or kW. A 7,000-9,000 BTU unit suits a bedroom; 12,000 BTU is for a larger living room or an attic under the roof. Bigger isn't always better, because a strong unit in a small room is noisy.

Single-hose units suck room air out through the hose, which pulls warm air back in through gaps. Dual-hose units take outside air for cooling and work more efficiently, but are rarer. Newer models use R290 (propane) as refrigerant.

Split-airco units with an outdoor unit are a different category: installing or moving one involves the refrigerant circuit and should be done by a certified installer, so a used split unit is rarely the bargain it looks like.

sections.heading: Test checklist
paragraphs: Ask the seller to run it in cooling mode for ten minutes before you arrive, or bring an extension cord to test outside.
bullets: Air from the front is clearly cold within a few minutes
Air from the exhaust hose is warm (that's the heat being removed)
Compressor starts with a click and a hum, no loud rattling
Exhaust hose has no tears and the end fittings are present
Window kit (raamafdichting) included, or budget EUR 20-30
Remote control works, all fan speeds and modes
Water tank or drain plug: no cracked plastic, no leaking
Filters at the back present and not full of dust

sections.heading: Brands and noise
paragraphs: Common brands in the Netherlands are Qlima, DeLonghi (the Pinguino series), Tristar, Princess, Inventum and Midea. DeLonghi units tend to be quieter and better built. Check the noise level on the spec sheet: mobile units are never silent, and for a bedroom a model around 50 dB or lower at low fan speed is much more pleasant.
The Midea PortaSplit and similar designs put the compressor in a separate unit outside the window, making them quieter indoors. They're newer and more expensive used.

sections.heading: Running costs and setup
paragraphs: A mobile airco uses roughly 0.8 to 1.3 kW while the compressor runs, depending on the model. Running it for a few hours a day in a heatwave is affordable; leaving it on all day adds up. Keep the exhaust hose short and as straight as possible, close the window kit properly, and shut curtains on the sunny side. In dehumidifying mode, empty the water tank regularly or attach a drain hose, because a full tank stops the compressor.

sections.heading: Timing and pricing
paragraphs: Prices follow the weather. In a heatwave, used units sell for close to new prices within hours. From September to March, the same units sit on Marktplaats for weeks. Buy in the off-season, test it then, and store it upright.

Transport it upright too; if it had to lie down, let it stand for a few hours before switching on. On vindje.com you can ask for a 'mobile airco with exhaust hose, at least 9000 BTU, quiet, under 150 euro within 20 km' and keep the air coolers out of your results.

faq.q: What is the difference between a mobile airco and an air cooler?
faq.a: An airco has a compressor and an exhaust hose and cools the air. An air cooler blows air over water and only cools slightly, while adding humidity.

faq.q: How many BTU do I need?
faq.a: Around 7,000-9,000 BTU for a bedroom and around 12,000 BTU for a larger living room or an attic room.

faq.q: Does a mobile airco need a window?
faq.a: Yes, the exhaust hose must go outside, usually through a window with a window seal kit.

faq.q: When is the best time to buy a used airco?
faq.a: In autumn and winter, when demand is low and sellers lower their prices.

example_wish: Mobile airco with exhaust hose and window kit, at least 9000 BTU, quiet for a bedroom, under 150 euro, within 20 km

title: Buying a used Thermomix: TM31, TM5, TM6 or TM7
meta_title: Buying a used Thermomix: versions and checks
description: Buying a used Thermomix: differences between TM31, TM5, TM6 and TM7, Cookidoo subscription, what to check on the blade, scale and heating, and fair prices.
intro: A used Thermomix can save you a lot compared to buying new from Vorwerk, but check which version you're getting and how its recipes work. Test the scale, the heating and the blade, and look closely at the bowl and lid seals, which are the parts that wear.

sections.heading: The versions
paragraphs: The TM31 (from 2004) has buttons and a dial, no screen with recipes. It still cooks, weighs and blends very well. The TM5 (2014) added a touchscreen and guided cooking with recipe chips (Cook-Keys) and later Wi-Fi. The TM6 (2019) has a larger screen, built-in Wi-Fi, more modes like slow cooking and sous-vide, and works with the online recipe platform Cookidoo. The TM7 (2025) has a new design, larger screen and a quieter motor.
Many TM5 accessories (bowl, Varoma) fit the TM6, but check before buying spare parts. TM31 parts are separate.

sections.heading: Cookidoo and guided recipes
paragraphs: On the TM6 and TM7, guided recipes come through Cookidoo, which needs a paid subscription after any free period. Without it, the machine still works manually, but you lose the step by step cooking that many people buy it for. Count that yearly cost in your comparison.

Ask the seller to remove the machine from their Cookidoo account and do a factory reset, so you can link it to yours. A TM5 can work with Cook-Keys and Cookidoo too, but its features are more limited.

sections.heading: What to check
paragraphs: Ask the seller to show the machine heating and blending. Bring a little water and a carrot or some sugar.
bullets: Scale: put a known weight on it (a 1 litre water bottle is about 1 kg) and check the reading
Heating: heat water to 100 degrees and watch the display climb
Blade unit: no wobble, no grinding sound, no rust or leaks under the bowl
Sealing ring of the blade: soft and intact (a new one is cheap)
Bowl base: no burnt-on residue or damaged contacts
Lid locks and the safety arms move freely
Touchscreen responds everywhere (TM5, TM6, TM7)
Accessories: Varoma, butterfly whisk, spatula, measuring cup, simmering basket

sections.heading: Common wear and repairs
paragraphs: The blade unit is the part that wears most. A leaking or noisy blade can be replaced, but a genuine one costs a fair amount. Heating problems can mean the bowl needs replacing, which is expensive. Vorwerk offers repairs, but at a price that makes a cheap used machine less cheap.
Machines used in a busy household for five or more years can still be fine. A TM31 that cooked daily for 15 years is more likely to need a blade and seal soon.

sections.heading: Questions to ask the seller
paragraphs: Ask these before you travel, so you can compare listings and skip the vague ones.
bullets: Which version is it, and when was it bought (a receipt helps)
Has the blade unit or sealing ring ever been replaced
Has it been repaired by Vorwerk or a third party
Is it removed from the seller's Cookidoo account
Which accessories and extra parts are included
Was it used daily or only now and then

sections.heading: Alternatives and odd listings
paragraphs: Lidl's Monsieur Cuisine and other cooking robots look similar but are different machines with different accessories, and they often appear in Thermomix searches. They're cheaper and fine for many people, but they're not a Thermomix and parts don't swap.

Be wary of a TM6 or TM7 far under market price with stock photos, and sellers who only ship. These are high-value items scammers like. If you want a specific version, say a TM6 with Varoma and an extra bowl under 750 euro within 30 km, vindje.com can filter that out of the many listings.

faq.q: Can you use a used Thermomix without Cookidoo?
faq.a: Yes. All functions work manually; you only lose the guided recipes on the screen.

faq.q: Which Thermomix version is the best value used?
faq.a: The TM5 is often the best value for cooking. The TM6 is better if you want guided recipes through Cookidoo and modes like slow cooking.

faq.q: Do TM5 parts fit the TM6?
faq.a: Many do, including the bowl and Varoma, but check the specific part before buying it.

faq.q: How do I know if the Thermomix blade is worn?
faq.a: A worn blade unit wobbles, makes a grinding noise or leaks under the bowl. Check it while blending.

example_wish: Thermomix TM6 with Varoma, removed from previous Cookidoo account, blade in good condition, under 800 euro, within 30 km

title: Buying a used robot vacuum: batteries, apps and docks
meta_title: Buying a used robot vacuum: what to check
description: Buying a used robot vacuum: Roborock, Roomba, Dreame and Ecovacs, app account unbinding, battery, lidar and dock checks, and fair prices.
intro: Robot vacuums lose value fast, so a two year old Roborock or Roomba can cost a third of its new price. The things to check are the battery, the app link to the seller's account and the self-emptying or mopping dock, which is where most of the money is.

sections.heading: Brands and features
paragraphs: Roborock is the most common brand on Marktplaats, from the budget Q series to the S8 and newer flagship models. Dreame, Ecovacs (Deebot), Xiaomi, Eufy and iRobot (Roomba) are also widely sold. Robots with lidar (a spinning turret on top) map the house accurately and clean in neat lines. Camera-based robots work well too. Cheap robots without mapping bounce around randomly and miss spots.
Mopping robots range from a simple wet cloth to rotating pads and docks that wash and dry the mops. Self-emptying docks save you from emptying the small bin after every run.

sections.heading: App account and cloud service
paragraphs: Most robots are linked to the seller's app account. Before you take it, ask the seller to remove the robot from their app and do a factory reset. If they don't, you may not be able to add it to your account. Test that you can connect it to your phone at the pickup if possible, or at least see it working in their app.
Check that the brand's app still supports that model. Smaller brands and very old models sometimes lose app or cloud support, which can leave a robot without mapping or scheduling.

sections.heading: Battery and runtime
paragraphs: A worn battery means the robot returns to the dock halfway through cleaning. Ask how long it runs on a full charge and how big the house is. Replacement batteries for popular Roborock and Roomba models are available for EUR 30-70, so a weak battery isn't a dealbreaker on a good robot, but it should lower the price.

sections.heading: Checklist at the pickup
paragraphs: Ask the seller to charge the robot fully before you arrive, then work through this list.
bullets: Robot starts cleaning from the app or the button
Lidar turret spins (if it has one), no 'laser sensor error'
Main brush and side brush turn; check for hair wrapped around the bearings
Wheels spin freely and spring back when pressed
Bumper clicks in all directions
Robot drives back to the dock and starts charging
Self-emptying dock: listen for the suction when the robot docks
Mopping dock: clean and dirty water tanks present, no smell or mould
Filter, dust bag and spare brushes included

sections.heading: Is a robot vacuum right for your home
paragraphs: Robot vacuums work best on open floors with few cables, toys and loose rugs. Thick rugs with long pile, high door thresholds (above about 2 cm) and dark carpets can confuse cheaper models. Most Dutch apartments suit them well. Before buying, think about where the dock goes: it needs a socket and some free space on both sides, and a large all-in-one dock is about the size of a small cabinet.

sections.heading: Docks, smells and parts-only listings
paragraphs: Mopping docks hold dirty water. If it was left standing, they can smell badly and grow mould. Look into the dirty water tank and the washing tray. Cleanable, but it tells you how the robot was looked after.

Listings for just a dock, or a robot without a dock, are common. A robot without its charging dock is not much use, and docks for flagship models are expensive. Parts-only robots ('defect', 'voor onderdelen') are mainly for people repairing the same model.
On vindje.com you can ask for something like 'Roborock with lidar and self-emptying dock, battery still runs an hour, under 250 euro within 20 km' and leave out the robots sold without a dock.

price_guide.item: Roborock Q7 or similar with lidar
Roborock S8 Pro Ultra or similar all-in-one
Robot for parts or without dock

faq.q: How do I remove a robot vacuum from the previous owner's account?
faq.a: The seller removes the device in their app and you then do a factory reset. Without that step, it may refuse to pair with your account.

faq.q: How long does a robot vacuum battery last?
faq.a: Often a few years of daily use. A worn battery shows as short runtimes; replacement batteries are available for popular models.

faq.q: Is a robot vacuum with a mop worth it?
faq.a: For hard floors, a robot with rotating mop pads and a washing dock does a decent job. Simple wet-cloth mops add little.

faq.q: Is a used Roomba still a good buy?
faq.a: It can be, but check that the app supports the model and that spare parts are available. Lidar robots from other brands usually map better at the same price.

example_wish: Roborock robot vacuum with lidar and self-emptying dock, battery runs at least an hour, removed from previous app account, under 250 euro, within 20 km

title: Buying a used stroller (kinderwagen): brands and checks
meta_title: Buying a used stroller in the Netherlands: what to check
description: How to buy a used stroller (kinderwagen) on Marktplaats: which brands hold up, what a fair price is, and the checks to do at pickup before you pay.
intro: A used stroller is one of the best second-hand baby buys: they get a year or two of use, the good brands are built to last, and new prices are steep. Stick to well-known brands with spare parts, check the fold, brakes and wheels in person, and budget for a new carrycot mattress.

sections.heading: Which brands are worth buying used
paragraphs: In the Netherlands the market is dominated by Bugaboo (Fox, Cameleon, Donkey, Bee, Butterfly), Joolz (Day, Aer, Hub, Geo), Mutsy (Evo, Nio, Icon) and Cybex (Priam, Balios, Mios). Easywalker, Thule and Babyzen (the Yoyo) are also common. These brands sell spare parts like wheels, tyres, handlebar foam and fabrics, which matters when a three-year-old pram needs a fix.
Cheaper supermarket or webshop brands can be fine for a second buggy, but if something breaks there is usually no part to order. On a used purchase that tips the balance toward the known names.

sections.heading: Combi, buggy or travel stroller
paragraphs: A combi kinderwagen comes with a carrycot (reiswieg) for the first months and a seat unit for later. Used listings often say 'compleet met wieg en zitje', which is what you want if the baby is not born yet. If your child already sits up, a lighter buggy or a compact travel stroller like the Yoyo or Bugaboo Butterfly is easier on Dutch trains and narrow staircases.

Check that the parts in the photos belong together. Bugaboo and Joolz have changed adapters and chassis between generations, so a Cameleon 3 seat does not fit a Fox frame. Search the full model name with the generation number.

sections.heading: Checks at the pickup
paragraphs: Push it around the room or the street for a minute. A good stroller rolls straight without you correcting it.
bullets: Fold and unfold it twice. It should lock with a clear click, without forcing.
Engage the brake and push hard. Both rear wheels should stay locked.
Spin each wheel. Wobble or grinding means worn bearings; flat or cracked tyres need replacing.
Press down on the handlebar to feel the suspension. Clunks point to worn joints.
Look at the handlebar foam or leatherette. Peeling is common and costs extra to replace.
Open every zip and buckle on the harness. A five-point harness must click shut on all points.
Check fabrics for mould spots, especially under the carrycot mattress and in the hood.
Ask what is included: rain cover, footmuff, sun canopy, car seat adapters, basket.

sections.heading: Mattress, fabrics and hygiene
paragraphs: Buy a new mattress for the carrycot. Used mattresses can hold moisture and mould, and they are cheap to replace compared with the stroller itself. Most Bugaboo and Joolz fabrics can be zipped off and washed, so ask the seller whether they have been and smell them at the pickup. A stroller from a smoking household is hard to get fresh again.
Stored in a damp shed or a garage over winter is a warning sign. Look for rust on the axles and on the folding joints.

sections.heading: Replicas and recalls
paragraphs: Look-alike strollers are sold online with designs very close to the Babyzen Yoyo and some Bugaboo models. A price far below the going rate, no logo on the frame and no serial number sticker are red flags. Genuine Bugaboos have a serial number label on the chassis, which also lets you check the brand's recall notices.
If the seller cannot tell you the model year, photograph the label and look it up before you pay.

sections.heading: Searching smarter
paragraphs: Sellers write titles like 'Bugaboo Fox 2 compleet zwart' or 'Joolz Day+ met wieg'. On vindje.com you can describe the whole thing at once, for example the model, that it should include the carrycot and a rain cover, and that you want it within 15 km, and listings that only sell the frame get filtered out.

price_guide.item: Bugaboo Cameleon 3 (Plus), complete with carrycot and seat

faq.q: Is it safe to buy a second-hand stroller?
faq.a: Yes, if the brakes, harness and fold lock work and the frame is not bent. Replace the carrycot mattress and wash the fabrics before use.

faq.q: Which stroller keeps its value best?
faq.a: Bugaboo and Joolz resell well in the Netherlands, so a used one you buy now can often be sold again for a good part of what you paid.

faq.q: Do I need a carrycot for a newborn?
faq.a: For the first months a baby should lie flat, so you need a carrycot or a seat that reclines fully flat and is approved from birth. Check the manual for the specific model.

faq.q: Can I buy Bugaboo spare parts separately?
faq.a: Yes, wheels, tyres, fabrics and handlebar covers are sold separately for most recent models, which makes a slightly worn used Bugaboo a reasonable buy.

example_wish: Bugaboo Fox 2 or Fox 3 complete with carrycot, seat and rain cover, no torn fabric, under 450 euro, within 20 km

title: Second-hand car seats: when it is safe and when to skip
meta_title: Second-hand car seats: when buying used is safe
description: Should you buy a used car seat (autostoeltje)? When it is safe, which labels to check (i-Size, R44), expiry dates, and when to walk away and buy new.
intro: A used car seat is only safe if you know its full history: no crash, not too old, all parts and the manual present. If a stranger cannot tell you that with confidence, skip it and buy new. Of all baby gear, this is the one where saving money is hardest to justify.

sections.heading: Why car seats are different
paragraphs: A car seat is designed to absorb one crash. After a collision the plastic shell and foam can have hairline cracks or compressed sections that you cannot see. Manufacturers tell you to replace a seat after any accident, even a minor one. A seller on Marktplaats has no reason to mention that their seat was in a fender bender, and you have no way of checking.
That is why the best used car seat is one from a family member or friend who can tell you exactly how it was used.

sections.heading: When buying used can be reasonable
paragraphs: Buying from a stranger is not automatically wrong, but every one of these should be true:
bullets: The seller can say when it was bought and states it was never in an accident.
The production date (stamped in the plastic, often under the seat) is less than about 6 years ago. Check the manual for the brand's own lifespan.
The approval label is present: R129 (i-Size) or R44/04.
The harness, buckle and adjusters work smoothly, and the straps are not frayed.
The shell has no cracks or white stress marks, especially around the belt guides and Isofix arms.
All parts are there: newborn insert, headrest, and the manual or the model name so you can download it.

sections.heading: i-Size, R44 and Isofix
paragraphs: Newer seats are approved under UN R129, called i-Size, and are grouped by the child's height rather than weight. Older seats carry the R44/04 label. New R44 seats are no longer sold in EU shops, but using one is still allowed. For a used purchase, an i-Size seat is the better pick because it will be newer and has passed a side-impact test.
